title: v0.8.0
body:
### Security

- **The unlock-code key has a random salt of each profile's own**
  ([#566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/566)). It used one fixed Argon2id
  salt for every install, so the work of attacking one stored config was shared across
  all users. A profile still in the old format is moved to the new one the first time it
  is unlocked, in a single store write that cannot leave it unopenable. Once moved, it
  cannot be opened by an earlier release.
- **Encrypted config blobs are bound to their profile**
  ([#569](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/569)). The secured config and the
  protected tier of `config.json` carry the profile name (and a format tag) as AES-GCM
  associated data, and each kind of blob has its own HKDF label, so a blob copied into
  another profile no longer opens there. Exports are bound to no profile and use the
  export label in the key derivation, as the docs already claimed. Older blobs and
  exports still open and are rewritten on the next save. Renaming a profile by hand now
  makes it unopenable; move one with export and import.
- **The activity log is encrypted** ([#568](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/568)).
  It names contacts, aliases and community DIDs and was stored in clear in `config.json`;
  it now lives in the encrypted tier, and an older config's log moves there when it is
  next opened. Every entry is stripped of control, bidi and zero-width characters and
  capped at 1024 characters as it is added, since many quote what a peer sent.
- **`config.json`, exports and startup-failure reports are written atomically and
  owner-only from creation** ([#567](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/567)). A
  crash mid-save leaves the previous file instead of a truncated one; a new profile
  directory is created `0700`; an export refuses to write through a symlink.
- **Secrets are held in wiping types on more paths**
  ([#570](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/570)): the Settings passphrase
  forms and their actions, the unlock code typed or read at start-up, the VTA session
  token from setup, and decrypted config plaintext. A vetting ticket's `Debug` output
  no longer shows its code or secret, and ticket codes are compared with `subtle`.

### Changed

- **The Fig release line.** `vta-sdk` 0.92, `affinidi-tdk` 0.49, `affinidi-messaging-sdk`
  0.50, `trust-tasks` 0.41, `dtg-credentials` 0.15 and `did-git-sign` 0.35 (and the
  matching VTI test crates), so this release talks to Fig VTAs and VTCs. DIDs are listed
  through the VTA's method-neutral `vta/dids/list`, so the setup probe sees a context's
  DIDs of every method and a context deletion's confirmation lists them all, not only
  did:webvh. Elections read with `vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7`. The build is pinned to Rust
  1.100.0 (`rust-toolchain.toml`); the minimum supported Rust stays 1.95.0.
- **A personhood presentation signs its challenge.** `proof.challenge` is now set as a
  signed proof option rather than added after signing: a Fig VTC (affinidi-data-integrity
  0.8.3 and later) hashes it with the proof configuration, so an unsigned one failed
  verification there. The challenge is still also written to `nonce`.
- **A change rebuilds only the panels that show it**
  ([#612](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/612)): the main page's sync from
  `Config` is split per panel (`sync_panels`), and each caller rebuilds the panels
  that read what it changed — an inbox task, a relationship, the vetting book, a
  community's favourite mark, a setting — instead of every panel. Startup, a load, a
  persona or membership change, the agent-name cache and inbound messages still
  rebuild them all. Text that changes with the clock alone — a credential turning
  "expired", a join awaiting its acknowledgement, a vetter grant expiring — was
  refreshed by whichever full rebuild came next; it is now refreshed once a minute
  (credentials, communities and vetting panels), so it is never more than a minute
  late. The vetting page's last two loop-side follow-ups are effect steps:
  reading requirements again plans the hidden-vetting challenge and the vetter pass
  as steps that run even after a refusal or a give-up, and Enter on the attestation
  form plans the hidden attestation or the enrolling pass. No visible change.
- **Vetting, Rooms, Elections and Repos use the reducer + effect shape too**
  ([#612](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/612)): each panel's handlers are a
  pure `plan` (no I/O, no awaits) that returns an ordered list of steps, and a runner
  that does the persona's key lookup and signing, claims the domain, applies what a
  started request changes only once the claim succeeds, spawns the job and saves —
  in the order the handlers did. The vetting page plans every action but reading
  requirements again and the attestation, which a loop-side pass still follows.
  No visible change.
- **The communities panel's context actions use the reducer + effect shape of the
  identity, relationship and inbox panels** (part of
  [#612](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/612)): a pure `plan` decides what a
  delete, device-access read, grant or revoke asks the VTA, and a runner claims the
  domain, spawns the job and only then marks the view busy. No visible change.
- **Context-path validation comes from vta-sdk**
  ([#610](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/610)): `vta_sdk::context_path` and
  `vta_sdk::identifier` replace the local copy, and accept and refuse exactly what it
  did, with the same messages.
- **The UI says *community* for a community and *VTC* only for the service behind it**
  ([#554](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/554)), as the README's glossary has
  it: the Communities and TSP panels label the community's DID "community", and the CLI
  help asks for "the community's DID".
- **Every vetting, repos, rooms and elections view, and every overlay, takes exactly
  the keys its footer lists** ([#580](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/580)).
  Vetting forms take Tab/↑/↓ only where there is another field, ←/→ only on a choice and
  Space only on a box to tick, and a key a form does not take says so instead of moving
  the focus off it. A list's verbs are listed and taken only when there is a row for
  them. Repos takes its "this machine" keys only where they apply to the highlighted
  repository; an overlay says which keys it does not take instead of swallowing them.
- **Joining a community no longer freezes the rest of the app**
  ([#529](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/529)). The join runs as a job on the
  main loop instead of a nested event loop, so saves, inbound messages, VTA supervision
  and timers carry on while it runs. Esc, F10 or an error cancels a resolve, discovery or
  launch at once, and the steps already taken are undone in reverse — except once the
  join request is being sent: then the exit waits for it, so the request is recorded and
  the persona the community now holds is kept. Messages from that community wait until
  the request is recorded, so a fast answer is not dropped. A join job that
  panics reports "Joining a community failed (internal error)."
- **The runtime loop is a `Runtime` struct with one method per event**
  ([#528](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/528)), and its arms are tested on
  their own. Rooms and elections share one community request/reply engine, and the
  replies awaited by thread are held in a `PendingReplies` table the runtime owns
  instead of three process-wide statics
  ([#534](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/534)). Every TUI save goes through the
  save scheduler, and background work is spawned through one `Job` / `dispatch` shape
  ([#535](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/535), in part).
- **Less work per loop turn** ([#555](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/555),
  [#556](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/556),
  [#565](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/565),
  [#557](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/557)). The published state is shared
  (`Arc<State>`) rather than copied three times a turn, and two idle timers no longer
  re-publish it. Config sync no longer reads did-git-sign's files or re-checks every VRC
  for post-quantum proofs; persona labels, membership counts and relationship keys are
  looked up by map. Personas load three at a time at startup, and one that fails no
  longer stops the rest (their progress lines can interleave). VTA retries are jittered,
  and `OPENVTC_DEBUG_LOG` is rotated once it passes 50 MiB.
- **CI runs the `#[ignore]`d end-to-end suites on every PR**
  ([#537](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/537)); CONTRIBUTING states when a
  test may be ignored.

- **One confirmation rule** ([#579](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/579)). A destructive or outward-facing action
  is armed by its key and committed by `y` alone; Enter — the key that opened the view —
  now cancels like any other key. Every prompt ends "y: confirm · any other key:
  cancel". Affected: community delete/leave/cancel-join, device-access revoke, Inbox
  dismiss/clear-all, relationship and credential remove, invitation credential
  delete/purge, agent-name remove, persona deletions, capability toggle, vetting
  abandon/delete-ticket/withdraw/decline, local-face delete, make-reusable and
  forget-contact. Typed-word confirmation stays for WIPE, RESET and context deletion.
- **Now confirmed** ([#579](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/579)): Inbox `r` (the rejection is sent to the peer),
  Settings "Remove the unlock code", and Communities `m` (issue VMC) and `R` (renew).
- **A key table per view, a `?` overlay, feedback for unused keys**
  ([#580](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/580)). Every main-page footer is drawn from the view's key table in one
  format (`key: does · key: does`, one key vocabulary); `?` lists exactly the focused
  view's keys and the global ones; a key a view does not take says "x does nothing here
  — ? lists this panel's keys" in the footer row. Help / Status's shortcut list comes
  from the same table.
- **Consistent keys** ([#580](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/580)): archive is `x` on the VTA invitation list (was
  `r`), show archived is `v` there (was `i`), refresh is `r` (was Tab); Communities
  joins with `n` (was `j`), and `j`/`k` move there and in the menu, as in rooms and
  elections. TSP Relationships takes ↑/↓ and Esc.
- **Text fields have a cursor** ([#578](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/578)). Every main-page form field is edited
  through `tui_input`: ←/→, Ctrl+←/→ and Home/End move within the field (they no longer
  switch panels), Backspace/Del delete either side, Ctrl+A/E/U/W/K edit, and no Ctrl or
  Alt chord types its letter. A paste is inserted at the cursor on the main page and in
  setup (it was appended on one and replaced the whole field on the other); the typed
  WIPE/RESET/DELETE words still take no paste.
- **The header names the class of a messaging failure** ([#585](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/585)): "✗ mediator
  unreachable", "mediator refused us", "mediator incompatible", "mediator not answering"
  … with "see Help". Help / Status shows the class, the full reason and what to do,
  and `r` there reconnects; so does Enter on the Settings mediator row. "Messaging
  unavailable" messages name the class and the remedy. The identity pane offers the
  holder-grant command only for a refusal, never for an unreachable agent.
- **Notifications** ([#584](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/584)): the Inbox badge counts what was sent to you, not
  your own pings and requests; Communities and Vetting carry badges of their own; the
  activity log draws errors and warnings in colour with a glyph.
- **Setup: Esc goes back** ([#588](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/588)) on every wizard page that has a page before
  it, keeping what was typed (it used to clear the field); choice pages say so. The
  setup DID is kept for the whole run, so going back and forward does not invalidate a
  PNM grant. The boxes no longer carry their own "Step x/y" counters beside the
  header's sections.
- **Wording** ([#554](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/554)): British spelling in the UI strings that were American;
  the profile's secret is the "unlock code" in Settings and the CLI as in setup; README
  glossary and CONTRIBUTING wording convention.
- **Status lines are typed** ([#577](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/577)): every panel's status carries a severity
  set by the code that produced it; the colour no longer comes from the wording.

- **Inbound dispatch and the join protocol live in `openvtc-core`**
  ([#530](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/530)). `process_inbound_message` and
  what it reports (`InboundEffects`, the off-loop `VerifyJob`s) moved from the CLI to
  `openvtc_core::inbound`; relationship-DID key creation to
  `openvtc_core::relationships::keys`; the join sequence's protocol steps (manifest over
  HTTP, context choice, submit transport, signed submit, pending record, persona
  rollback) to `openvtc_core::join::sequence`, and the join status poll to
  `openvtc_core::join::status_poll`. The TUI and `openvtc community join` now send a join
  through the same code. `openvtc community join` prints a line when the submit goes
  over a different transport than the community prefers, as the TUI already did.
- **One registry decides which inbound message types are accepted and who handles them**
  ([#531](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/531)). The transport's accept gate
  and the dispatcher are both derived from `openvtc_core::inbound::registry`, so a
  handler cannot exist for a type the gate drops. The gate no longer admits whole
  namespaces no handler claims (any `spec/vtc/*`, the legacy `openvtc/vtc/*` authority,
  any `linuxfoundation.org/openvtc/*`): those messages were already ignored by the
  dispatcher as unknown, and are now dropped at the gate instead, still logged at `warn`.
- **Remote failures carry a typed class** ([#536](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/536)).
  A VTA call that fails now reports whether the VTA was unreachable, timed out, refused
  our credentials, answered in a shape this client cannot read, did not know the thing,
  refused with a reason, or failed on its side — in the message (e.g. `VTA timed out:
  …` where it used to say `VTA Error: …`) and as data. Startup's "couldn't reach the
  VTA" guidance follows the class.
- **Library API** (`openvtc-core`, additive unless noted): `inbound` (`process_inbound_message`,
  `apply_inline`, `InboundEffects`, `ThreadedReply`, `VerifyJob`, `PreVerified`,
  `Arrival`, `Deferred`, `registry::{ROUTES, Family, TypeMatcher, Route, classify}`);
  `relationships::keys`; `join::sequence`; `join::status_poll`; `vta_task::{retry,
  retryable, MAX_ATTEMPTS}`; `capabilities::CAPABILITY_TYPE_PREFIX`;
  `OpenVTCError::Remote` with `RemoteService`, `RemoteKind`, `ErrorClass`,
  `OpenVTCError::{vta, remote, class, remote_kind}` and `errors::class_of`;
  `DiscoverError::kind` and `MessagingError::class`; a `test-support` feature (test-only
  hooks). **Removed:** `didcomm::OPENVTC_CATCH_ALL_PATTERN` (the gate is the registry
  now; `didcomm::routes_inbound_type` still answers whether a type is admitted). Errors
  that were `OpenVTCError::Vta(String)` from VTA calls are now `OpenVTCError::Remote`.

- **Faster startup, sends and `health`** ([#557](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/557),
  [#559](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/559),
  [#560](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/560)). A persona's VTA-held keys are
  fetched concurrently, and relationship keys at most 8 at a time. TSP discovery shares
  one DID resolver, so its cache is used, and the status-list and manifest HTTP clients
  are built once. `openvtc health` resolves and probes up to 4 parties at once, and still
  prints them one at a time.

- **The OS keyring is written only when the secured config changed**
  ([#564](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/564)), not on every save: fewer
  Keychain prompts, Secret Service round trips and, on token profiles, card touches.
- **Library API** (breaking for code that uses `openvtc-core` as a library):
  `UnlockCode` now holds the code and derives against the stored salt, and
  `Config::unlock_code` is the new `UnlockKey`; `SecuredConfig::save` takes an
  `UnlockKey`; `ProtectedConfig::save`/`load` take a `ProtectedBinding`;
  `PublicConfig::logs` is now the read-only `legacy_logs`, with the log in
  `ProtectedConfig::logs`; `passphrase_encrypt_v2` and its `_blocking` form are
  replaced by `passphrase_encrypt` and `passphrase_encrypt_blocking`, which write the
  `OPV3` format.
- **Backup import writes the secured config before the config file, and only gives a
  profile an unlock key when it is protected by an unlock code.** An import of a
  plaintext-protected backup used to write a passphrase-sealed secret the next load
  refused.
- **`OpenVTCError` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`** (breaking for code that uses
  `openvtc-core` as a library). A `match` on it outside `openvtc-core` needs a
  wildcard arm. From now on a new error variant is not a breaking change, so a
  fix that needs one can be backported to a release branch as it is.

### Fixed

- **Rooms: an acceptance that cannot start says why**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). When the persona's key lookup or
  the request failed, the "busy" note replaced the real reason; the reason is now shown,
  and "busy" only when the lane is busy.
- **Rooms: accepting while a request is still unanswered is refused, not left stuck**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The acceptance was set to
  "Collecting" with nothing sent, and stayed there. The press now changes nothing and
  says "A request to this community is still waiting — try again when it answers.",
  as Elections refuses the same case.
- **Rooms: a step whose key lookup fails is given up, not retried every tick**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). A follow-on step (a page read,
  an acceptance step, a renewals check) whose persona key could not be read was retried
  and its error rewritten on every tick. It now shows the reason once and stops until
  the person acts again, as Elections does.
- **Repos: a failing forge-link check is reported once and backs off**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). A link-status poll that kept
  failing (the persona's key, the send, or no answer) repeated its error every 5 s. A
  failure is now said once until it changes or a poll is answered, and each failure in a
  row doubles the wait before the next poll, up to 60 s; the panel shows the current
  interval. A send that failed or a poll that went unanswered was silent before and is
  now said too.
- **Vetting: a vetter request that cannot be built leaves nothing behind**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). If the request document failed
  to build after the request was prepared, the prepared request stayed in the
  application as though sent. It is now forgotten, as it already was when the signing or
  the send failed.
- **Vetting: a submission-challenge request that cannot be signed is un-filed**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). When the persona's key lookup or
  signing failed, the challenge question stayed filed as though asked until its reply
  window ran out. It is now un-filed, as it already was when the send failed.
- **Vetting: a hidden attestation with no VTA connected says so, not "busy"**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). Attesting the hidden way with no
  VTA session said the hidden-vetting work was busy. It now says the VTA is not connected
  and the request stays open; "busy" is said only when the VTA is busy.
- **Six messages no longer show a long run of spaces mid-sentence**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). A line of text wrapped in the
  source without its trailing `\` carried the next line's indentation into the message:
  the hidden-vetting key-recovery mismatch, the identity panel's "worlds apart" warning,
  three wallet join messages (session expired, unreadable answer, no answer) and the
  unreadable directory-disclosure failure. A source check now catches the mistake.
- **Vetting: a session that cannot be opened leaves the request as it was**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). When the persona's key lookup or
  signing failed, the request stayed in an open session in memory (not saved) that no
  applicant ever received; it is now put back where it stood. And when the question
  asking the community for its requirements could not be sent, the page still counted
  it as asked, so the next Enter opened the session without the requirements; it now
  asks again.
- **Vetting: a decline or withdrawal that cannot be built is undone**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). If the decline or withdrawal
  document failed to build, the request stayed declined, or the statement marked
  withdrawn, in memory with nothing sent. Both are now put back, as they already were
  when the signing or the send failed.
- **Hidden vetting: an enrolment or draw that cannot be signed is un-filed**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). When the persona's key lookup or
  signing failed, the enrolment question, and a draw's question and in-flight record,
  stayed in the book as though sent until the reply window ran out. They are now taken
  back, as a failed send already did, so the schedule asks again on its next pass.
- **Vetting: starting an application while another vetting send runs says it started**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The application was saved, but
  the busy warning replaced "Application started.", so it read as refused. The status
  now says it started and that its requirements wait until the other send finishes (m
  asks then).
- **Vetting: refreshing a hidden application while busy keeps the busy refusal on screen**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). `m` on a hidden-vetting
  application while another vetting send ran refused the requirements question, but the
  submission-challenge request that follows replaced the refusal with "Asking the
  community for a submission challenge…". The challenge is still asked, quietly, when
  the requirements were refused or failed.
- **Hidden vetting: "get tokens" (`d`) no longer covers a failure with its summary**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The per-community summary was
  shown after the vetter pass even when the pass had just said a warning or an error
  (a question to a community that could not be sent), which hid it. The failure now
  stays on the status line; the summary is shown otherwise.
- **Hidden vetting: a key-binding question that cannot be signed is un-filed**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The question asking a community
  which hidden-vetting key it bound you to stayed filed as though sent when the signing
  failed. It is now un-filed, as a failed send already did; it is asked again after the
  usual re-ask interval.
- **Rooms: a refresh on a busy lane says so**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). Opening the panel or pressing `r`
  while another Rooms request held the lane read nothing and said nothing, so an empty
  panel sat at "asking the community…" indefinitely. It now says the lane is busy and to
  press `r` once it finishes, including on the loading screen.
- **Rooms: renewals collected before the VTA disconnected are no longer retried for ever**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The step handing them to the VTA
  was kept and retried on every tick while no VTA was connected. It is now dropped; the
  first read once a VTA is connected collects the renewals again.
- **Elections: opening an election on a busy lane changes nothing but the status**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The refused press still reset
  which community the view reads from and the membership it presented. Those now change
  only once the read is under way.
- **Elections: a list refresh on a busy lane says so**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). Opening the panel or pressing `r`
  on the list while another Elections request held the lane read nothing and said
  nothing. It now says the lane is busy and to press `r` once it finishes, including on
  the loading screen. The VTA's held election notifications are still read: they come
  from the VTA on a lane of their own.
- **Repos: saving the workspace settings no longer blocks the app on the disk**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). Saving the settings form checked
  the directory and wrote the settings file on the event loop, and opening the panel read
  the file there too. Saving is now a workspace job, shown as running while it writes,
  and refused while another workspace job (which may write the same file) runs; opening
  reads the file on the blocking pool.
- **Repos: an unreadable workspace settings file is said when the panel opens**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). The warning that the settings
  could not be read (and the defaults are used) was cleared at once by the read the
  panel starts, so it was never seen. It is now shown after that read starts.
- **Hidden vetting: enrolment, draw and key-binding failures are logged**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). A hidden-vetting enrolment or
  token draw that could not be signed, and a key-binding question that could not be sent,
  were shown only on the status line, so the next status replaced them. They now go to
  the activity log too.
- **Vetting: the VTA context chosen for an application's face is saved**
  ([#614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/pull/614)). Choosing, making or wearing a
  face, or sending a card, picked the application's VTA context and kept it in memory
  without saving it, even when the press was then refused as busy. The context is now
  kept only once the job goes ahead, and saved with it; a card whose key lookup fails
  takes it back.
- **A vetting send no longer starts alongside one already running**
  ([#609](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/609)). A vetting step the app sends on
  its own (a refresh, a hidden-vetting step, a grant check) freed the vetting busy-guard
  when it finished, even while a send the person started still held it, so a second
  press could start a second send. Background work the app starts on its own now frees
  only what it claimed.
- **Headless commands say what the `OPENVTC_*` trust-anchor overrides did**
  ([#611](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/611)). `community join`, `repo …`,
  `signing …` and `setup --vta-did` applied the overrides silently; they now print each
  ignored variable (release builds refuse trust-anchor overrides) and any applied
  override to stderr, as the TUI shows them in its activity log.
- **The identity forms draw the caret where the cursor is**
  ([#578](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/578)). It was always drawn at the end
  of the text, though ←/→ moved the cursor; a choice (the value type) shows none.
- **Ctrl+V pastes a ticket link into "Ask a vetter" again, and `y`/`u` copy the code and
  link on the full-screen ticket** ([#580](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/580)).
  Both were listed but did nothing.
- **A failed join submit no longer deletes a persona the join reused**
  ([#529](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/529)). Only a persona the join itself
  minted is rolled back.
- **A standalone persona mint is written to disk in one save**, including its origin
  context ([#535](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/535)), and the save no longer
  blocks the event loop.

- **Nothing essential is clipped at 80x24** ([#576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/576)): all twelve menu items fit
  (the activity log shrinks to 4 rows below 32 rows; the menu scrolls to the selection
  on anything shorter, and is wide enough for its longest item); the footer row leads
  with `F10: quit` and `?: keys` and keeps only whole hints; setup step 1 scrolls to
  every PNM command and shows the copy result in its footer row.
- **A ping reports its result** ([#584](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/584)) in the Relationships panel — the pong
  and its latency, or "No reply to the ping after 30 s" — and an unanswered ping's
  outbound task is expired instead of sitting in the Inbox.
- **Keys that did nothing silently now say so, and keys a footer did not list are gone
  or listed** ([#580](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/580)): e.g. Inbox `a` on a task with nothing to accept, `d` on
  a membership credential, VTA `u` on an active invitation, persona `d` on a persona in
  use, letters in the identity pane's read-only views and pickers.
- **The masked passphrase length counts characters**, not bytes ([#578](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/578)).

- **Setup and backup import refuse an unlock code shorter than 8 characters**
  ([#574](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/574)). Every unlock path already
  required 8, so a profile set up with a shorter code could never be opened again. A
  profile that already has a short code now unlocks, with a prompt to set a longer
  one under Settings -> Protection.
- **Setting an unlock code no longer freezes the screen**
  ([#563](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/563)). The ~1 s key derivation in
  setup and backup import now runs off the render task.
- **Hardware-token Factory Reset asks first** ([#575](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/575)).
  It names the card (identifier and manufacturer), warns when that card protects the
  profile, and erases it only after `RESET` is typed. With more than one card connected
  it refuses rather than picking one.
- **Failure messages are no longer drawn in success green**
  ([#577](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/577)). A status message worded as a
  failure ("Couldn't …", "… unavailable", "… not available", …) is red; any other message
  uses the plain text colour instead of green.
- **Export asks for the passphrase twice; passphrase forms say why Enter did nothing**
  ([#586](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/586)). Export Config has a
  confirmation field, and Export and Change Protection report an empty, short or
  mismatched passphrase instead of ignoring Enter. The Import form's footer no longer
  says "export".
- **Startup diagnostics name commands that exist**
  ([#581](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/581)): `openvtc setup` (not
  `--setup`), Restore Backup in setup, and Settings -> Protection. `--profile` is now
  accepted after a subcommand too (`openvtc health --profile work`).
- **`openvtc health --json` writes only JSON to stdout**
  ([#583](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/583)). The profile notices go to
  stderr. The interactive interface no longer starts when stdin or stdout is not a
  terminal; it points at the headless commands instead.
- **SIGTERM and SIGHUP shut down like F10** ([#587](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/587)):
  the terminal is restored, the last change saved and the profile lock released. A panic
  now also turns bracketed paste off and shows the cursor again. F10 is heard on the
  join screen while a DID resolves. A quit you asked for no longer prints "exited per user
  request"; other exits explain themselves on stderr.
- **An agent name is shown only after this device has verified it**
  ([#571](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/571)). Claiming, parking, resuming or
  removing a name no longer caches a hand-formatted `host/@name` as verified; it forgets
  the cached name so the background sweep re-verifies it. A name that arrives through VTA
  state sync is kept but not displayed until the sweep has verified it here.
- **Community and ballot-box answers are read up to 2 MiB**
  ([#558](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/558)). The join-manifest and
  ballot-box fetches no longer buffer whatever a peer-advertised endpoint sends.
- **The ballot box is reached under the public-hosts policy in every build**
  ([#573](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/573)); `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`
  no longer relaxes it. DID labels in `openvtc health` and rebuilt communities'
  sub-context ids are now derived with `didwebvh-rs`; a community whose DID has no path
  is named by its SCID instead of `host%3Aport`.
- **Typing an agent name waits at most 15 s** ([#562](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/562)),
  and the join screen says it is resolving.
- **Sending a message no longer holds the messaging identity lock while the recipient
  resolves** ([#561](https://github.com/OpenVTC/openvtc/issues/561)).
- **Peer messages are handled only as the sender the transport authenticated.** The
  inbound dispatcher used to fall back to a message's `from` header when the transport
  bound no sender to it (anoncrypt DIDComm, or an authcrypt whose `from` its sealing key
  does not back). A VRC request, a VRC request rejection, a trust ping or pong, a
  relationship rejection or finalize, and a notification are now acted on only when the
  `from` header names the DID whose key sealed the message; anything else is dropped with
  a log line before any handler runs. The same rule applies to messages handled by the
  headless `join` and `repos` commands. A pong now closes only a ping we sent, on its
  thread, to the party that answers it; a pong with no authenticated sender closes
  nothing. The answer to a ping, and the receipt a notification is answered with, go only
  to an authenticated sender. **Behaviour change:** a peer that sends these messages
  anoncrypt, or a pong with no sender, is no longer answered or acted on; a ping task
  answered that way stays in the inbox until dismissed. Every service in the stack already
  sends authcrypt.
- **A VRC received from a peer is checked in full before it is offered for storage.** Its
  subject must be the DID we use in that relationship, it must be inside its validity
  window (`validFrom` / `validUntil`), and where it names a `credentialStatus` the
  issuer's status list must establish that it is not revoked or suspended — a status that
  cannot be established refuses it, as for a credential a community issues. These join the
  proof and issuer checks it already passed. Accepting one from the inbox checks its window
  again, so one that lapsed while waiting is not stored. A received VRC is now filed under
  the relationship's key (the peer's persona DID) rather than the relationship DID that
  issued it, so the relationship view lists it and removing the relationship removes it;
  ones filed the old way are moved at load, and when the account sync brings one in from
  a device on an older build.

- **A wrong unlock code now gets another try.** At start-up the unlock prompt only
  rejected codes shorter than eight characters. A wrong code of full length left the
  prompt on the first try and failed afterwards, while the secured config was being
  decrypted, with a message about decryption and no second chance in that session.
  The five-attempt limit and the delay after the third miss, listed under 0.2.0, never
  applied to a wrong code. Each code is now checked against the stored config at the
  prompt: a wrong one says "That unlock code didn't work" and asks again, with the limit
  and delay applied. After the last attempt, or when a code given with `--unlock-code`
  or `--unlock-code-file` is wrong, it says how to recover an account kept by a VTA if
  the code is forgotten. The limit is there for typos and starts again when you restart.
  It does not protect against guessing; the cost of Argon2id for each guess does that,
  including for anyone who copies the stored config and guesses offline. Reported
  through the security process.

title: chore(release): v0.8.0
body:
GA of the 0.8 (Fig) release, prepared by **Prepare a release** (`ga`) on `release/0.8`: `RELEASE` 0.8.0-rc.0 -> 0.8.0 and `## [Unreleased]` becomes `## [0.8.0] - 2026-11-24`.

The workflow pushed this branch but could not open the PR (no `RELEASE_TOKEN`: GitHub Actions may not create PRs here), so it is opened by hand; the commit is re-signed, content unchanged.

Merging it is the release: `release-tag.yml` tags `v0.8.0` and `publish.yml` publishes `openvtc-core` and `openvtc` 0.8.0.

title: docs(adoption): add first-use RAHP specification tutorial
body:
Closes #49

## What changed

Adds a consumer-facing, step-by-step tutorial over the existing retained-source TRQP examination. The tutorial shows the complete upstream sequence from bounded assurance question through affected contexts, source pinning, local risk hypotheses, replay observations, review/evidence binding, validation, fail-closed behavior, interpretation and reassessment.

It does not introduce a new review contract, canonical risks, downstream pressure-test semantics or an assurance decision engine.

## Artefact IDs affected

None. No canonical `data/` or `method/` records are changed.

Documentation and regression coverage only:

- `review/examples/standalone-trqp/TUTORIAL.md` (new)
- `tests/test_first_use_tutorial.py` (new)
- `README.md` (first-use navigation)
- `review/examples/standalone-trqp/README.md` (navigation/accuracy)
- `ADOPTION.md` (first-use route)

## Provenance — what triggered this change?

Issue #49. The existing upstream retained-source TRQP example is technically complete enough to reproduce, but its README primarily serves as a technical reference. The downstream RAHP Toolkit demonstrated the value of a sequential worked example. This contribution adapts that usability lesson to the canonical upstream review/evidence contracts without importing downstream-only schemas, identifiers or controller semantics.

The tutorial was substantially AI-assisted and then checked against the current upstream files, validators, retained outputs and contribution guidance. Independent human review remains required.

## Validation output

The PR workflow completed successfully. The added regression executed the documented replay, review validation, composed examination and deliberate mutable-revision failure.

```
PASS · 43 RK · 66 CT · 21 GR · 21 AT · 37 M · 36 US · 33 SC · 21 EPIC · 16 PERSONA · 9 REC · 3 RA · 3 GP · 0 errors · 32 warnings
```

The 32 retained corpus warnings are the existing task-force work queue and are not introduced by this documentation tranche.

## Assurance and compatibility

- The retained TRQP source, review record, evidence sidecar, risk source and replay implementation are unchanged.
- No schema, vocabulary, corpus, API or governance semantics change.
- Documentation explicitly separates machine validity, evidence integrity, reviewer inference, assurance judgment and governance authority.
- A successful replay remains `overall_assurance: review-required`.
- The tutorial includes affected people/contexts and plausible harm before risk selection.
- The negative exercise uses the repository's existing invalid mutable-revision fixture.
- Local-link and command regression coverage is intended to prevent obvious documentation drift.

## Out of scope / residual evidence

- No claim of TRQP deployment assurance or full conformance.
- No risk scoring, risk acceptance or governance decision.
- No general evidence-sidecar standardization.
- No downstream CRK mappings, portable-pattern identifiers, pressure-test controller or rendered-output machinery.
- Independent methodological review is still required.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 tools/validate.py` exits 0
- [x] Every new/changed record has a `provenance` block (not applicable: no canonical records changed)
- [x] New guardrails have an assurance test; new controls reach a metric (not applicable)
- [x] No generated file under `build/` was edited by hand
- [x] If a risk score changed, the evidence for the change is stated above (not applicable)
- [x] DCO/CLA and required CI checks pass on the current head
- [ ] Independent review complete


### First-use review response (11 November 2026)

Addressed the four bounded onboarding corrections from [Nicky's first-use feedback](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/50#issuecomment-5859216573): the tutorial now explains RAHP and its output, uses a Python virtual environment with an Ubuntu `python3-venv` note, explains how to obtain and use the full immutable target commit ID, and is discoverable directly from the root README. title: build(deps): generate the vti-specs crates with trust-tasks-build 0.2.2
body:
Moves the `vti-specs-*` generator from `trust-tasks-build` 0.1.4 to 0.2.2.

0.2 (trust-tasks-tf #1243) keeps only the `$defs` each `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` reaches. That dropped `vtc/storage/credentials/set`'s `SealedCredentialCleartext`, which `vtc-service`'s sealed-credential check reads, and the OpenAPI components `vta_sdk::openapi` renders, so VTI stayed on 0.1.4. 0.2.2 ([trust-tasks-tf #1353](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1353)) keeps every definition a specification declares and references from nowhere.

- `Cargo.toml`: `trust-tasks-build = "0.2.2"`.
- `Cargo.lock`: the 0.1.4 and 0.2.1 copies are replaced by a single 0.2.2.
- `deny.toml`: drops the `trust-tasks-build:<0.2` skip.

The bindings regenerate in each `vti-specs-*` `build.rs`. CI runs the `SealedStorageCredential` cleartext check and the `openapi_snapshot` test against them.

Release notes

Sourced from dtg-credentials's releases.

Banyan

Coordinated OpenVTC release Banyan — a known-good, cross-project snapshot of all OpenVTC projects. Tagged at the main-branch HEAD on 2026-06-23.

Changelog

Sourced from dtg-credentials's changelog.

[0.14.0] - 2026-11-10

Breaking: a VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, context v2), and verify_chain holds a chain to them — see Changed (breaking) below.

Added

  • A VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, Purposes of Use; trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84). credentialSubject.purposes is optional, {"scope":"any"} or {"scope":"listed","purposes":[...]} with a non-empty list of registered names or absolute IRIs, each once; absent means any, and any never grants modelTraining. dtg_credentials::purposes::PurposeScope models it, read strictly (an any carrying purposes, an empty list or a duplicate is refused at parse). A VAC stating it lists DTG_CONTEXT_V2 (https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v2) second, which is now recognized beside v1; a VAC stating it under v1 is refused.
  • verify_chain enforces the chain rule and reports the effective purposes. A link stating none takes its parent's; a link stating purposes its parent does not grant is AuthorityError::WidensPurposes. The root states the grant, so only a root naming modelTraining can pass it on. VerifiedAuthority::purposes carries the result.
  • DTGCredential::with_purposes states them (switching the context to v2), and with_purposes_under refuses at issue purposes wider than those the parent states.

Changed (breaking)

  • CredentialSubjectAuthority gains purposes, VerifiedAuthority gains purposes, and AuthorityError gains WidensPurposes; DTGCredentialError gains InvalidPurposes (non-exhaustive).

  • did:scid parties are matched by their DID. Chain verification (verify_chain, delegation chains) and the acknowledgement/acceptance pairing compare an issuer, subject, presenter, governing party or principal by DID, ignoring a did:scid ?src= locator (VTI-KEY-160): did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=a.example and did:scid:vh:1:<scid> are one party. A did:scid and its did:webvh log are still two. Every other DID compares as before. A proof's verificationMethod is still bound to its issuer exactly.

  • Depends on affinidi-did-common directly (already in the graph through affinidi-data-integrity).

Security

  • DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key now refuses a proof that was not made by a key of the credential's issuer. It verified the signature under the key it was handed but never checked that the proof's verificationMethod belongs to issuer, so a caller that resolved the method the proof names and then trusted issuer() accepted a credential naming any issuer, signed by anyone. It now returns DTGCredentialError::ProofNotFromIssuer, as verify_grant_with_public_key already did; the two share one check. A method belongs to the issuer when the DID before its # is exactly the issuer, when it is the issuer itself, or when it is a bare #fragment (read against the issuer — verify_grant_with_public_key previously refused that form). The comparison is verbatim. A caller signing with a key whose id is not a method of the issuer will now see its own credentials refused; give the signing secret the issuer's method id.

title: chore(deps)!: move to the Fig line (vta-sdk 0.92, affinidi-tdk 0.49, trust-tasks 0.41, did-git-sign 0.35); pin Rust 1.100.0
body:
Moves openvtc to the Fig release line: vta-sdk 0.92, affinidi-tdk 0.49,
affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.50 (-delivery 0.3, -core 0.1.15), trust-tasks-rs /
capability-client 0.41, trust-tasks-build 0.2.1, dtg-credentials 0.15,
did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.35, affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.9,
affinidi-did-web 0.2, affinidi-status-list 0.2, agent-names 0.2,
didwebvh-rs 0.8.3; dev: vta-service 0.85, vti-vetting-pcs 0.25,
vti-voting 0.21, test-mediator 0.55.

API moves:
- list_dids_webvh is gone (VTI #2763): the setup probe lists a context's
  DIDs of every method through vta/dids/list; rebuild lists did:webvh and
  did:scid (scid:vh) personas.
- The context deletion preview's webvhDids is now dids (every method).
- UpdateAclRequest gains purposes (left unchanged).
- affinidi-status-list 0.2's StatusPurpose is non-exhaustive and not Copy:
  use its as_str().
- MockVta and the transport harness moved to vta-test-support (VTI #2730),
  a first-party VTI crate on the same vta-service line.
- vta/pcs/voter/read 0.6 -> 0.7 (adds the tombstone read; re-pinned with
  trust-tasks add, generated by trust-tasks-build).

Cleanups:
- Pin the toolchain to Rust 1.100.0 (rust-toolchain.toml), as VTI does;
  CI installs the pin, and the MSRV job keeps 1.95.0 via RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN.
- Remove the deprecated DIDCOMM_EVENT_CHANNEL_CAPACITY (its rationale stays
  as a comment), the unused MainPanel::switch and NavResult::None, and the
  allow(dead_code) on TaskKind: Informational carried a string nothing read.
- Delete tasks/archive/ (in git history; the two docs that linked it say so).

The config migrations are untouched.

Supersedes Dependabot #621.

title: trust-tasks-build-v0.2.2
body:
### Fixed

- **build,rs,ts,ts-gen,go,dart**: Keep the free-standing $defs a specification declares in the request schema constant ([#1353](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1353))

#1243 pruned every root $defs entry the request root does not reach. That also
  dropped definitions a specification declares for clients and references from
  nowhere, such as vtc/storage/credentials/set's SealedCredentialCleartext, which
  travels only inside a seal. VTI reads it, and the OpenAPI components its console
  uses, out of PAYLOAD_SCHEMA, and so stayed on trust-tasks-build 0.1.

  The request constant now also keeps each free-standing definition (one other
  than Response that no #/$defs/<name> reference anywhere in the schema names)
  and what it references. A shared definition spliced in from another document is
  always referenced, so it is still pruned when only the response uses it. The
  response document keeps only what it reaches.

  Applied in all seven generator copies and re-derived in check-bundles from
  defOrigins; regenerated, five specifications change in all four languages.

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.41.0` → `0.41.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.41.0` → `0.41.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.31.3` → `0.31.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` | npm | `0.2.2` → `0.2.3` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.13.5`) | `0.13.4` → `0.13.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.4`) | `0.1.3` → `0.1.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.3` → `0.12.4` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

body:
Bumps [vta-sdk](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure) from 0.87.0 to 0.88.1.
Release notes

Sourced from vta-sdk's releases.

vta-sdk-v0.88.1

Fixed

  • vta/vtc/voting-service: Follow-ups to #2676, #2677 and #2678 (#2684)

  • fix(vta,vtc): keep no copy of further bearer-bearing responses for redelivery

    Follow-up to #2677.

vta-sdk-v0.88.0

Added

  • vtc: A VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID (#2698)

  • feat(vta-sdk): vtc-host-classical, the VTC template a level-1 did:webs can carry

    A level-1 did:webs holds one key-state signing key, and CONVENTIONS.md 0.2 §9.2 refuses vtc-host's second (post-quantum) signing slot as keyAlgorithm and forbids a VTA to drop what a template describes; the template keys block has no optional slot (vta/did-templates/* 3.1). So a did:webs VTC (VTI-KEY-001) names a template that does not ask for the key: vtc-host-classical, vtc-host less the pq-signing slot, its verification method and its assertionMethod reference. It is derived from vtc-host when loaded, not shipped as a second file, so the two cannot drift (pinned by a test rendering both). The §9.2 check is unchanged: vtc-host stays refused, every other refusal stands.

    The §9.2 service rule reads a {DID}#… id as the DID's own fragment: a service supplied whole as a variable (SERVICE_TSP, SERVICE_DIDCOMM) keeps the placeholder, because a whole-value substitution is not substituted again, and was refused under did:webs as "not a fragment".

  • vta: Provision an integration as a did:webs (#2695)

The template var DID_METHOD=webs routes provision-integration's mint to create_did_webs: level 1, class service (VTI-KEY-192), shaped by the template with every CONVENTIONS.md 0.2 §9.2 check and refusal, gated by [dids] webs_service_dids, and published at WEBVH_SERVER (required: a did:webs has no serverless mode) on WEBVH_DOMAIN under WEBVH_PATH. No wire member is added to provision/integration/0.3: the method is a template var, as DID_METHOD=scid already was. A build without webs refuses the selection by name.

The bundle stays SealedPayloadV1::TemplateBootstrap. Its keys are the key-state key and the designated X25519 key agreement key under the ids the did:webs document gives them (#), config.did_document is the document the stream derives, and the stream itself rides a new TemplateOutput::WebsKeriCesr in place of a did.jsonl. It is emitted only for a did:webs, so every webvh/did:key/did:peer bundle is byte-identical; an opener that predates the variant refuses such a bundle by name. title: chore(deps): Bump trust-tasks-build from 0.1.3 to 0.2.0
body:
Bumps [trust-tasks-build](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf) from 0.1.3 to 0.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from trust-tasks-build's releases.

trust-tasks-build-v0.2.0

Added

  • rs,build: A generated file names the runtime contract it needs (#1253)

trust-tasks-rs gains a hidden __private::ABI_V1, and every file trust-tasks-build generates for an application opens with const _: () = ::trust_tasks_rs::__private::ABI_V1; under a comment naming the trust-tasks-build version. A runtime too old for the generator, or one that has moved to a newer contract, now fails on that line with an error naming the contract, instead of on whichever hidden door the generated code reaches first (#1101). The in-repo prebuilt tree is unchanged.

  • rs,build,ts,ts-gen,go,dart: Emit only the $defs each schema constant reaches (#1243)

  • feat(rs,build,ts,ts-gen,go,dart): emit only the $defs each schema constant reaches

    Each generated request and response schema constant now keeps only the root $defs its root reaches: the request drops Response and what only the response uses, the response document drops what only the request uses. Registry bundles are unchanged, so no pinned digest moves. Types are still generated from the whole schema.

    trust-tasks-rs packages at 10,037,990 bytes (9.57 MiB) against 10,349,753 (9.87 MiB) before.

  • rs: No prebuilt specification families by default (#1240)

trust-tasks-rs and the trust-tasks facade now have default = []. A plain dependency compiles the runtime and the framework's own trust-task-* modules, not every deprecated prebuilt family (a ~17 GB build). A consumer that still uses specs::<family> enables features = ["all-specs"], or the one family it uses.

Fixed

  • build,cli: Require a spec slug and version for every locked task, and the canonical path for every index entry (#1245)

An official lockfile entry's slug and version were checked only against a Type URI built from the same strings, then used as path segments of the vendored bundle's location. Each entry's slug and version must now have their SPEC form, whichever registry it comes from. The CLI now also requires an index entry's path to be //bundle.json, the only form the registry publishes.

trust-tasks-build-v0.1.4

Documentation

  • RELEASING describes the Dart downgrade leg as it now behaves; trust-tasks-build README uses cargo add (#1225)
  • Fix drifted counts, release runbook, licences and stale examples across the four libraries (#1224)

  • docs(getting-started): move the worked example to acl/grant/0.3 and stamp issuedAt with issued_at_now()

    The example pinned acl/grant/0.2, superseded by 0.3, and stamped issuedAt with chrono::Utc::now(), the full-precision form #970 removed from the libraries. The TS consumer example wrote toISOString() milliseconds into document fields the same way. body:
Bumps [trust-tasks-rs](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf) from 0.39.0 to 0.40.1.
Release notes

Sourced from trust-tasks-rs's releases.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.40.1

No release notes provided.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.40.0

Added

  • messaging: Wake a device through its own mediator, and end-to-end delivery receipts (#1297)

Two gaps in getting a document to a device that is on another mediator or has no agent of its own.

Waking (messaging/wake/set 0.1, messaging/wake/request 0.1):

  • messaging/wake/set: an account gives its own mediator the opaque WakeHandle its push gateway issued, or clears it (absent = clear). The mediator never holds a token. Response { wakeCapable }.
  • messaging/wake/request: a sender that has just queued mail for a DID asks that DID's mediator to ring, naming the queued messages by their stored ids (<= 8). Contentless. The mediator rings (push/wake, as itself) only when the account has a handle, every id is queued for it, fresh (10 min) and undelivered, the stored sender is the requester where the envelope reveals one, the requester is not blocked, the account is offline, no id has rung before, and per-(sender, addressee) and per-addressee limits hold. Requests may arm for 120 s. The response is always {} so it is not a presence oracle. Proof REQUIRED.
  • push/register 0.3: selfControl lets a device with no controller VTA register as its own controller, with an initial allowlist (normally its mediator), under gateway policy (push/register:selfControlRefused). Exactly one of controllerVtaDid / selfControl.
  • push binding 0.1 (draft, in place): §3.5 sender-requested, mediator-triggered wake; self-controlled handles in §3.3.

Receipts (messaging/receipt 0.1, TSP binding 0.2):

  • messaging/receipt: a fire-and-forget Trust Task { confirms } the recipient's delivery layer sends to the transport-authenticated sender once it durably holds a message that asked for a receipt. Requested, never automatic; may be declined; settles only from the addressed party; never answered. title: vtc-service-v0.33.0
body:
### Build & CI

- **deps**: Move to the affinidi-tdk 0.49 generation, mediator 0.55 and trust-tasks 0.41 ([#2796](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2796))

* build(deps)!: move to the affinidi-tdk 0.49 generation, mediator 0.55 and trust-tasks 0.41

  The whole workspace moves together, as the generations do not mix:
  affinidi-tdk 0.49 with affinidi-crypto 0.4, affinidi-encoding 0.2,
  affinidi-data-integrity 0.9, affinidi-secrets-resolver 0.6,
  affinidi-did-common 0.5, affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.9,
  affinidi-did-resolver-traits 0.2, affinidi-did-webs 0.14, affinidi-tdk-common
  0.8, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.50, affinidi-messaging-didcomm 0.16,
  affinidi-messaging-delivery 0.3, affinidi-status-list 0.2, affinidi-bbs 0.5;
  the mediator crates 0.55 (test-mediator, mediator-admin, mediator-tui);
  trust-tasks-rs and its bindings 0.41 with jsonwebtoken 12; dtg-credentials
  0.15; agent-names 0.2; didwebvh-rs 0.8.3; jsonschema 0.61; heapless 0.9.4;
  plus the minor/patch bumps of the dependabot group (pgp, kube, rmcp,
  google-cloud-auth, …). The enclave proxy's resolver moves to 0.9 with it.



### Fixed

- **vtc-service**: Issue the approver invite to an administrator made under a waiver (VTI-APV-022) ([#2795](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2795))

An administrator made in single-administrator mode got no step-up approver
  enrolment invite. The invite was minted only when a parked action reached its
  threshold; a waived operation never parks, and `record_waived` wrote its
  history entry with `approver_invite: None`. The new administrator was left
  with no factor to answer a step-up with, contrary to
  `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md` §3.1a.

  `record_waived` now mints the same invite once the history entry is saved,
  for the same operations the threshold path does (an unrestricted grant, not
  an admin invitation), and the requester collects it once from the entry as
  before. The anchor VTI-APV-016 asks for is the requester's operation-bound
  step-up, which the waiver already required.

- **vtc**: A network that refuses the community is not one that does not list it ([#2791](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2791))

`vtc/networks/preview` and the join path read every refusal of the
  community's own-entry read (`vtn/entries/show`) as "not listed". A VTN
  that could not resolve a did:webs community's DID answered
  `permissionDenied`, and the console told the administrator to ask for an
  invitation the network had already sent, greying out Join, with the real
  reason in parentheses.

  The VTC now classifies the read: not listed only when the network
  answers "no entry" (`taskFailed` with `details.reason: not_found`, a
  bare `notFound`, or a declared `…:notListed`); an invalid listing; a
  refusal; or no answer. The preview carries the classification in
  `ext."org.openvtc".listingProblem` (its response schema has no member
  for it), and join and the other writes report a refusal as
  `networkRefused` and no answer as `unavailable` instead of `notListed`.

  The console shows a refusal or no answer as an error: what happened,
  the network's reason in full, and a hint when the network cannot
  resolve the community's DID method. Join stays disabled either way.

title: vtc-audit-v0.4.0
body: ### Added - **vtc-service**: Store and serve an uploaded community logo ([#2751](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2751)) * feat(vtc-service): store and serve an uploaded community logo A community can now upload its logo, and the VTC serves it from its own origin, so it shows in the console, the member portal, both sign-in pages and the default landing page wherever the VTC is hosted. Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. What it adds: - `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1` (pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`): an administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one re-encoding at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - `GET /v1/community/logo`: public, like `public-profile`. Served from memory against a small record read, with a fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - A `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - Console: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. Design note: docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md.
author: stormer78

title: vtc-client-v0.47.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vtc-mcp**: Tell the person to paste a sign-in link and type the number (VTI-LNK-105, VTI-LNK-107) ([#2794](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2794))

`vtc_sign_in` told the person to open the trigger link "in the browser that
  holds their wallet". The bridge has no page on the community's portal, so a
  wallet that sees the click holds it to the portal's origin and refuses it as
  `wrong-origin` (VTI-LNK-105); with the browser wallet, neither the member nor
  the admin audience could be completed that way. The link is now to be
  pasted into the wallet (the browser wallet's popup, "Open a link from your
  assistant", vta-browser-plugin#450) or scanned with a phone wallet.

  It also said the wallet "shows a number too" for the person to compare. It
  does not: the wallet asks the person to type the number the starter shows,

The invite was minted only when a parked action reached its threshold; a waived operation never parks, and `record_waived` wrote its history entry with `approver_invite: None`. The new administrator was left with no factor to answer a step-up with, contrary to `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md` §3.1a. `record_waived` now mints the same invite once the history entry is saved, for the same operations the threshold path does (an unrestricted grant, not an admin invitation), and the requester collects it once from the entry as before. The anchor VTI-APV-016 asks for is the requester's operation-bound step-up, which the waiver already required. - **vtc**: A network that refuses the community is not one that does not list it ([#2791](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2791)) `vtc/networks/preview` and the join path read every refusal of the community's own-entry read (`vtn/entries/show`) as "not listed". A VTN that could not resolve a did:webs community's DID answered `permissionDenied`, and the console told the administrator to ask for an invitation the network had already sent, greying out Join, with the real reason in parentheses. The VTC now classifies the read: not listed only when the network answers "no entry" (`taskFailed` with `details.reason: not_found`, a bare `notFound`, or a declared `…:notListed`); an invalid listing; a refusal; or no answer. The preview carries the classification in `ext."org.openvtc".listingProblem` (its response schema has no member for it), and join and the other writes report a refusal as `networkRefused` and no answer as `unavailable` instead of `notListed`. The console shows a refusal or no answer as an error: what happened, the network's reason in full, and a hint when the network cannot resolve the community's DID method. Join stays disabled either way.

Release notes

Sourced from jsonschema's releases.

[Python] Release 0.61.2

Fixed

  • References inside a registered resource resolving against the URI it was registered under instead of its $id. #1862

Performance

  • Validation of deeply nested instances against recursive schemas takes time linear in their nesting depth.
  • unevaluatedProperties next to if, dependentSchemas, anyOf or oneOf checked in one pass over the object by is_valid, without validating those subschemas again.
  • Validation of Python instances checks the common value types inline.
  • propertyNames validating each str key itself instead of a new string built from its text.
  • allOf branches that only check properties, required or type: object checked in one pass over the object by is_valid.
  • required beside properties and additionalProperties: false checked in the same pass over the object by is_valid.
  • $refs to a subschema another $ref already compiled dispatched once instead of twice.
  • unevaluatedProperties matching property names by their first and last bytes instead of hashing them.
  • additionalProperties that only checks type decided without entering the subschema for each value by is_valid.
  • Literal-prefix patterns rejecting a property name on its first byte before comparing the rest.
  • Integer const and enum values compared directly instead of through their decimal forms.
  • Root dictionary keys checked with one type comparison each before validation.

Release notes

Sourced from affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin's releases.

v0.53.0

Changed — the vta feature is back

  • affinidi-messaging-mediator depends on vta-sdk 0.90 again, released on the same line as this workspace (affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47 / affinidi-tdk 0.45 / trust-tasks 0.39 / affinidi-crypto 0.3), so every affinidi-* and trust-tasks-* crate still resolves once.
  • vta (VTA-backed key management: operating secrets fetched from a Verifiable Trust Agent at boot, periodic refresh, mediator rotate-admin) is back in the mediator's default features, and enabling it no longer stops the build. Library consumers can still turn it off with default-features = false; self-hosted mediators never used it.
  • mediator-setup's vta feature is now real and on by default: the VTA step offers full setup, admin-only and offline export again, the deployment defaults pick a VTA-managed setup again, and --setup-key-out, --setup-key-file, use_vta = true recipes (sealed-mint, sealed-export, --bundle) and did_method = "vta" run instead of exiting 5. A self-hosted did:webvh document is rendered by vta-sdk's didcomm-mediator template again. A wizard built with --no-default-features and without vta keeps the previous release's behaviour (only "No VTA", VTA paths refused with exit 5).
  • The build commands the wizard renders (Dockerfile, cargo install, cargo build) list the mediator's vta feature again.
  • The container image includes VTA integration again: the mediator's default features (with vta) and mediator-setup with its vta flows. A VTA-linked deployment that stayed on an earlier image can move to this one.

  • vta (VTA-backed key management: operating secrets fetched from a Verifiable Trust Agent at boot, periodic refresh, mediator rotate-admin) is back in the mediator's default features, and enabling it no longer stops the build. Library consumers can still turn it off with default-features = false; self-hosted mediators never used it.
  • mediator-setup's vta feature is now real and on by default: the VTA step offers full setup, admin-only and offline export again, the deployment defaults pick a VTA-managed setup again, and --setup-key-out, --setup-key-file, use_vta = true recipes (sealed-mint, sealed-export, --bundle) and did_method = "vta" run instead of exiting 5. title: chore(deps): update trust-tasks-https requirement from 0.39 to 0.40 in /fuzz
body:
Updates the requirements on [trust-tasks-https](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from trust-tasks-https's releases.

trust-tasks-https-v0.40.0

Build & CI

  • https: Jsonwebtoken 11 in trust-tasks-https, jsonschema 0.60 in trust-tasks-rs (#1290)

Aligns the two dependencies a downstream workspace (OpenVTC VTI) compiles twice because these crates pinned older majors: jsonschema 0.49 in trust-tasks-rs (validate feature) beside its 0.60, and jsonwebtoken 10 in trust-tasks-https (jwt feature) beside its 11.

jsonschema is private to trust-tasks-rs (no jsonschema type is in its public API) and needed no code change. jsonwebtoken is public through JwtBearerAuth::new(DecodingKey, Validation, _), so a consumer that builds those values with jsonwebtoken 10 must move to 11: a break of the jwt feature's API, hence the !. No source change was needed in this crate.

Fixed

  • rs,https,ts,go,dart: Refuse a document that marks an unrecognized ext namespace critical (#1256)

  • fix(rs,https,ts,go,dart)!: refuse a document that marks an unrecognized ext namespace critical

    SPEC §4.5.2 rule 4: a consumer that does not recognize a namespace named in extCritical MUST NOT process the document and MUST reject it with unsupportedExtension. No runtime read the member, so a document whose payload type does not model it was processed as if the namespace were absent.

    Each runtime gains a check (check_critical_extensions, checkCriticalExtensions, CheckCriticalExtensions) that walks the payload as received alongside its schema, applies rules 1, 2 and 4, and runs in every consume pipeline after the proof and per-specification checks and before the item-11 record. The recognized namespaces are a new consume-checks option, empty by default. Shared vectors in fixtures/consume/ext-critical.json pin the four together.

Changelog

Sourced from trust-tasks-https's changelog.

release-plz — versioning, changelogs and publishing for the Rust workspace.

The model: merge PRs to main freely. scripts/release-pr.sh runs

release-plz update on every push to main and keeps a single "Release PR" up

to date with the version bumps and changelog entries those merges imply.

Merging THAT PR is the release — release-plz release tags each crate and

publishes to crates.io. release-plz no longer opens the PR itself (see below).

So merging a feature PR never releases anything, and a release is a reviewable

diff rather than a side effect of a merge. See RELEASING.md.

WHAT GETS PUBLISHED is decided in each crate's Cargo.toml, not here. Every

workspace crate publishes except those that set publish = false:

trust-tasks-codegen (the internal generator) and the example applications. release-plz honours that flag — it still updates an

unpublished crate's version and dependency requirements so the workspace stays

coherent, it just never uploads it. Keeping the decision in the manifests

means cargo and release-plz cannot disagree about it.

The npm, Go and Dart packages are NOT here: release-plz is Rust-only and has

no hook that could bump trust-tasks-ts/package.json. scripts/release-pr.sh

bumps them with scripts/release-bump-{ts,go,dart}.sh, built to work the same

way, and commits them into the same Release PR as the crates.

[workspace]

Changelog entries come from conventional commits via git-cliff. The commit

message IS the entry, so there is nothing for two concurrent PRs to conflict

over — which is what the per-PR "add a CHANGELOG entry and bump the version"

ritual used to cost.

changelog_config = "cliff.toml"

OFF: the crates' public APIs are checked on every pull request instead

(rs API compatibility in rust.yml, scripts/check-rs-api-compat.sh), each

against its own last release, and an undeclared break is refused there. That

leaves the bump to the conventional commits, as for the npm, Go and Dart

packages: a ! scoped to a crate (or a BREAKING CHANGE trailer) moves the

compatibility field, anything else is a patch.

It was on, and run here, until the Release PR job outgrew it: cargo-semver-

checks builds rustdoc JSON twice per crate, and over every generated family

trust-tasks-rs peaks at ~12.6 GB. The job took 8-13 minutes after every merge

to main, was repeatedly killed for memory on a 16 GB runner, and found a

break only after the PR that made it had merged. On the PR the check covers

the runtime plus one generated family and takes about a minute; the script's

header says why that is enough.

semver_check = false

One GitHub Release per published crate, carrying that crate's changelog

section. This is what an external consumer lands on from crates.io.

git_release_enable = true

  so the TSP account/update document is built with its type URI named rather
  than read off the SDK payload; deny.toml lists trust-tasks-rs 0.40 until
  they move to 0.41.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(vtc-service): issue the approver invite to an administrator made under a waiver (VTI-APV-022)
body:
## Problem

In single-administrator mode, granting someone community-admin worked but gave them no step-up approver enrolment invite. The requester's history entry for the grant had no `approverInvite`, and the new administrator was left with no approver to answer a step-up with.

The invite was minted only on the threshold-completion path (`admin_actions::complete`, after a parked action is approved). A waived operation never parks. `record_waived` wrote the history entry with `approver_invite: None` and never called `invite_new_administrator`. That contradicts `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md` §3.1a: "Every administrator made by a completed action … is issued an approver enrolment invite automatically."

## Fix

- `record_waived` saves the history entry and then, if the operation made a new unrestricted administrator, mints the same invite onto it. The requester collects it once from `vtc/admin/actions/show`, as on the consent path.
- Both paths now use one predicate, `makes_new_administrator`: a `GrantUnrestricted` act that isn't an admin invitation.
- The VTI-APV-016 anchor is the requester's authority exercised under their own operation-bound step-up, which the waiver already requires. No new trust is introduced.
- Docs: `admin-access.md` §3.1a and the step-up design note §6c now cover the waived case.

## Tests

- New: `single_admin_mode::vti_apv_022_a_waived_new_administrator_is_issued_an_approver_invite`. It checks that the invite is on the waived history entry, is shown once, and is audited as `invited`. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: everything passes except four console-bundle tests. Those failed only because I ran with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`, and pass when rerun with the bundle built.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `scripts/check-docs.py` all pass.

## For a community already affected

An administrator already made under a waiver doesn't get an invite retroactively. Issue one by hand: Members → the member → **Invite to enrol an approver** (`auth/step-up/approver/invite`).

Updates `serde-saphyr` from 2.1.1 to 2.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from serde-saphyr's releases.

2.2.0 Compatiblity release

This release includes non-breaking changes accumulated while preparing for 3.0.0, which will include breaking changes to tag handling, number formats with underscores, and other corner cases.

Added

  • Added opt-in Options::null_as_string (default: false) to preserve plain null, Null, NULL, ~, and empty scalars as text for string targets in both mapping keys and values, including String, &str, and Cow<str> (#267). Explicit !!null tags remain rejected for strings; Option<T>, untyped null inference, mapping-key comparison, and no_schema quoting requirements keep their existing behavior.
  • Added Options::bom_inside_document_as_content (default false) to preserve a BOM at the start of a token inside a document as plain scalar content, including in included YAML. A BOM in a document prefix is still skipped.

Fixed

  • Preserve uppercase radix prefixes (0X, 0O, 0B, including signed forms) as strings during implicit type inference, including untagged enums and flattened fields (#266). Direct typed integer parsing, explicit !!int tags, and mapping-key comparison retain their existing behavior.
  • Infer plain signed not-a-number spellings (+.nan, -.NaN, -.NAN) as strings during implicit type inference, since the YAML 1.2 Core schema allows a sign on .inf only (#271; #272, #273). This applies under every NonFiniteFloatPolicy, including untagged enums and flattened fields. Also accept these spellings without quotes when no_schema: true for string values and mapping keys, including String, &str, and Cow<str>. Direct untagged float targets continue to accept them as NaN. Explicit !!float scalars now preserve the supplied NaN sign when deserialized as floats.

Changed

  • Updated to granit-parser 2.2.0. Under-indented quoted scalar continuations in block context and tabs before quoted continuations are now accepted by default; strict_indentation: true continues to reject them.
