title: fix(vtc-mcp): tell the person to paste a sign-in link and type the number (VTI-LNK-105, VTI-LNK-107)
body:
## Problem

A user setting up vtc-mcp couldn't complete `vtc_sign_in` with the browser wallet, for either the `member` or the `admin` audience. Two parts of what the bridge told them were wrong:

1. **"Open it in the browser that holds their wallet."** The bridge has no page on the community's portal. A wallet that sees the click holds it to the portal's origin and refuses it as `wrong-origin` (VTI-LNK-105). The browser wallet also had no paste entry for sign-in links. That is fixed in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#450.
2. **"The wallet shows a number too … approve only if the two are the same."** The wallet doesn't show a number to compare. It asks the person to type the number the starter shows, and the community checks `auth/oob/prove`'s `enteredNumber` against the request's match number (`vti-oob-server/src/tasks.rs`, VTI-LNK-107).

## Change

Text only, no behaviour change:

- `vtc_sign_in`'s `next` says to paste the link into the wallet (the browser wallet's popup, **Open a link from your assistant**) or scan it with a phone wallet, and not to click it in a tab.
- `vtc_sign_in_finish`'s `claimed` result says to have the person type the match number, and never to type it or approve for them.
- The tool descriptions, the operator guide `docs/03-vtc/vtc-mcp.md` (embedded and served as `vtc://guide/vtc-mcp`), `skills/vtc-community/SKILL.md`, the crate CLAUDE.md, the `signin.rs` module doc and the `SignInPoll::Pending` doc now agree. The step-up section also mentions the popup's paste box.

## Depends on

OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#450 adds the paste path for `sign-in` links. Until that ships, the browser-wallet half of the new instruction doesn't work. The phone-wallet path is unchanged, and an administrator can still use `vtc_enrol_signing_key`.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `python3 scripts/check-docs.py`
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-mcp -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-mcp`: 50 passed

title: fix(vtc-mcp): tell the person to paste a sign-in link and type the number (VTI-LNK-105, VTI-LNK-107) (#2794)
body:
fix(vtc-mcp): tell the person to paste a sign-in link and type the number (VTI-LNK-105, VTI-LNK-107) (#2794)

`vtc_sign_in` told the person to open the trigger link "in the browser that
holds their wallet". The bridge has no page on the community's portal, so a
wallet that sees the click holds it to the portal's origin and refuses it as
`wrong-origin` (VTI-LNK-105); with the browser wallet, neither the member nor
the admin audience could be completed that way. The link is now to be
pasted into the wallet (the browser wallet's popup, "Open a link from your
assistant", vta-browser-plugin#450) or scanned with a phone wallet.

It also said the wallet "shows a number too" for the person to compare. It
does not: the wallet asks the person to type the number the starter shows,
and the community checks it (`auth/oob/prove`'s `enteredNumber` against the
request's match number, VTI-LNK-107). The tool results, descriptions, the
operator guide (served as vtc://guide/vtc-mcp), the skill and the
`SignInPoll::Pending` doc now say "type", and never to type it for them.

Release notes

Sourced from EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action's releases.

Release 2.1.2 - cargo-deny 0.21.0

Fixed

  • PR#893 resolved #892 by correctly handling url matching when using IP hosts.
  • PR#895 fixed an issue where --target could not be passed multiple times in the CLI.
  • PR#885 resolved #772 by not emitting diagnostics for unused workspace dependencies when those crates were explicitly excluded from the graph by the user.
  • PR#887 resolved #707 by ignoring renamed packages when checking for workspace duplicates.
  • PR#902 resolved #898 by adding the unmatched-allow-build-script and allowed-crate-without-build-script diagnostics.
  • PR#911 resolved #910 by visiting each crate once when checking build-time dependents, so a dependency cycle no longer overflows the stack.
  • PR#915 resolved #914 by ignoring a trailing slash when exactly matching source urls, so that licenses.private.ignore-sources can match sparse registries.

Added

  • PR#899 resolved #896 by searching for configuration in .config as well.
  • PR#904 resolved #754 and #889 by adding 3 new configuration fields:
    • advisories.ignore-expiry - The default duration after the publishing of an advisory that an advisories.ignore will function for it. Once the current date surpasses that expiry the ignore will not prevent the diagnostic for the advisory being emitted. This also accepts an absolute date.
    • advisories.ignore.expiry is the same as the above, but scoped to a particular ignore. This value overrides the default.
    • advisories.ignore.allow only allows specific crates by PackageSpec to depend on the crate(s) that the advisory applies to, intended to prevent new crates or versions from being added to the graph that increase the number of edges and thus making it harder to update/remove the affected crate.
  • PR#906 changed the diagnostics for advisories and yanked crates to conditionally show the (try cargo update -p <affected crate>) and instead detect if any dependents use 1 or more version requirements that preclude updating to an unaffected/patched/unyanked version.

Deprecated

Release notes

Sourced from cborg's releases.

v7.0.0

⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

  • json: validate numeric fractions and exponents
  • json: cborg/json sorts map keys by UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units.
  • encode: encoded float16 subnormals that are not powers of two (multiples of 2^-24 below 2^-14) are now a 3 byte f9 item, not 5 bytes. Anyone hashing or comparing those bytes sees different output.

title: fix(vta-service)!: remove the unverified step-up approval token signer
body:
Closes #2702.

**For review, not auto-merged: this is security-sensitive.**

## What #2702 found
`vta-service/src/operations/step_up_approval.rs` signed a VTA approval JWS (`iss` = VTA, `sub` = holder, `aud` = RP) after a user-verification gate, `step_up_policy_approve`, that always returned `true`. The VTA's signature claimed a human had approved a step-up when nobody had been asked.

## What I found
That module has had **no callers since #1739** (2026-09-26). #1739 deleted the legacy DIDComm step-up approval handler that called it (`handlers.rs`, the `authorize_holder` / `build_vta_approval_token` call sites), but left the module behind. So the unverified signer isn't reachable today. It was dead code, and a trap for anyone wiring it back in.

The live step-up path is `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.5` and `approve-response/0.7` in `trust_tasks/step_up.rs`, and it **does** verify the user:
- **One gate:** the response must carry exactly one evidence kind the request offered (`accepts`). Once the approver has an enrolled passkey, only `webauthn` is offered.
- **The webauthn gate:** the assertion must be made by one of the approver's passkey verification methods, over the minted challenge, with **UV required** (`VerifierConfig::from_public_url(.., true)` → `vti-webauthn` rejects a clear UV flag).
- **The did-signed gate:** an `assertionMethod` proof by the approver's own key. It's offered only to approvers with no passkey enrolled.
- **Single use:** the challenge is consumed on first presentation (`consume_pending_step_up`).

## This PR
- **Removes** `operations::step_up_approval`, so no unverified VTA-signed approval can be minted.
- **Rewords** the doc comments in `operations/vault/mod.rs` that referred to it.
- **Adds** a handler test, `webauthn_step_up_refuses_no_uv_wrong_challenge_and_replay`, that pins the live gate:
  - an assertion **without UV** is refused (`assertionInvalid`), with the session left at aal1;
  - a UV assertion over **another challenge** is refused (`assertionInvalid`);
  - a UV assertion over the minted challenge **elevates** to aal2;
  - **replaying** that accepted approval is refused (`challengeUnknown`).

## Client impact
- **Wire:** none. No client sent the removed DIDComm message after #1739. iOS (#29) and the browser plugin use approve-request 0.5 / approve-response 0.7, which are unchanged.
- **API:** breaking for the `vta-service` library. The `operations::step_up_approval` module is removed; nothing in the workspace used it.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
affinidi-webvh-service still has the RP-side verifier for this token (`did_hosting_common::server::didcomm_unpack::verify_vta_approval_token`). With no producer left, that verifier is probably dead too.

fix(vta-service)!: remove the unverified step-up approval token signer (#2793)

`operations::step_up_approval` signed a VTA approval JWS ("this VTA
approved a step-up for `sub` at `aud`") after a user-verification gate,
`step_up_policy_approve`, that always returned true (#2702). Its only
caller, the legacy DIDComm step-up approval handler, was deleted in #1739
when every DIDComm and TSP request moved to proof-bound Trust Tasks.
Since then nothing has called it, but any future caller could have
handed out a VTA-signed approval with no human behind it. Remove the
module rather than leave that trap in place.

Step-up today is `auth/step-up/approve-request/0.5` and
`approve-response/0.7` (`trust_tasks/step_up.rs`), and it does verify
the user: the response must carry exactly one evidence kind the request
offered, either the approver's own `assertionMethod` proof or a WebAuthn
assertion by one of the approver's passkey verification methods,
verified against the minted challenge with the UV flag required
(`VerifierConfig::from_public_url(.., true)`). The challenge is consumed
on first presentation. A new handler test pins this down: an assertion
without UV, an assertion over another challenge, and a replay of an
accepted approval are each refused and elevate nothing; a user-verified
assertion over the minted challenge elevates to aal2.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_service::operations::step_up_approval`
(`authorize_holder`, `step_up_policy_approve`,
`build_vta_approval_token`, `load_vta_key0_signing_key`) is removed. It
had no callers in this workspace.

Closes #2702

title: fix(sign-in): open a pasted sign-in code from the popup (VTI-LNK-105 – 107)
body:
## Problem

An assistant over `vtc-mcp` signs its own key in as the person with `vtc_sign_in`, which hands the person a `sign-in` trigger link. With the browser wallet, neither the `member` nor the `admin` audience could be completed:

- the bridge has no page on the community's portal, so the link can't be clicked there, and a click anywhere else is `wrong-origin` (`sign-in-flows.ts`, `!origin || !originMatchesPortal(...)`);
- the popup's paste box accepted `step-up` links only.

A user setting up vtc-mcp hit exactly this and had to fall back to enrolling a signing key through the console.

## Why this is spec-conformant

VTI-LNK-105 binds "a reader that **recorded** the origin of the page the link was activated from". A pasted code has no recorded origin, which is the footing of a code scanned with a camera. In that case the spec relies on the number the person enters (VTI-LNK-106 / 107 don't apply). The wallet was stricter than the spec here.

## Change

The popup box (`OpenPastedLink`, now `RUNTIME_PASTED_LINK`, extension pages only) also takes a `sign-in` link. It opens the sign-in window with a flow record carrying **`pasted: true` and no origin**. For such a flow:

- **Nothing is skipped.** The confirm screen is shown even for one identity, with a note that the code was pasted. No click on the portal stands for the go-ahead (VTI-LNK-106).
- **The person types the number.** No page number is waited for or taken (`pageNumber` drops it; `handleTriggerLinkNumber` skips pasted records). The person enters the number the assistant shows, and the community checks it (VTI-LNK-107).
- **Only a community already in the records.** A pasted code for an unknown site returns `not-member`, with no join or hosting offer and nothing sent.
- **No origin is pinned.**

`pasted` is an explicit flag set only on the popup path. A click whose origin went missing is still `wrong-origin`, and a pasted flow that carries an origin is refused.

`RUNTIME_STEP_UP_LINK` is renamed to `RUNTIME_PASTED_LINK` (`vta-wallet/pasted-link`). The step-up behaviour is unchanged. CLAUDE.md has a new section on the pasted sign-in path.

## Tests

- `sign-in-flows.test.mts`: a missing origin without `pasted` is still `wrong-origin`. A pasted code keeps the confirm screen and sends nothing before Continue. A pasted code never takes a page number: it reaches `enter-number` at once even with a 60 s page wait, and the grant still names the verified portal origin. Pasted with an origin is refused. Pasted for an unknown community or DID host returns `not-member` with nothing sent.
- `sign-in-view.render.test.mts`: a pasted confirm with one identity is not auto-claimed and shows the note.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and the extension suite pass (1573/1573).

Companion change: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2794 updates `vtc_sign_in`'s instructions to say "paste it into the wallet popup".

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network calls
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the flow record is session storage, as before
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): internal extension message renamed, all senders and receivers updated; no wire change to the community
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a missing origin without the explicit `pasted` flag still refuses
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a lost worker loses the session-stored flow, and the person pastes again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

[0.61.2] - 2026-11-12

Fixed

  • References inside a registered resource resolving against the URI it was registered under instead of its $id. #1862

Performance

  • Validation of deeply nested instances against recursive schemas takes time linear in their nesting depth.
  • unevaluatedProperties next to if, dependentSchemas, anyOf or oneOf checked in one pass over the object by is_valid, without validating those subschemas again.
  • allOf branches that only check properties, required or type: object checked in one pass over the object by is_valid.
  • required beside properties and additionalProperties: false checked in the same pass over the object by is_valid.
  • $refs to a subschema another $ref already compiled dispatched once instead of twice.
  • unevaluatedProperties matching property names by their first and last bytes instead of hashing them.
  • additionalProperties that only checks type decided without entering the subschema for each value by is_valid.
  • Literal-prefix patterns rejecting a property name on its first byte before comparing the rest.
  • propertyNames reusing one buffer per thread for the names it checks instead of allocating one per object.
  • propertyNames on the jsonb instance representation reusing one buffer per thread for the names it checks.
  • Integer const and enum values compared directly instead of through their decimal forms with arbitrary-precision.

v0.51.0

Added — did:webs

  • The mediator resolves did:webs, so a did:webs client can authenticate and a did:webs recipient can be routed to. Requires affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.47, which does not turn on serde_json's preserve_order for the whole build. A mediator configured to resolve through a DID resolver cache server needs one that resolves did:webs (affinidi-did-resolver-cache-server 0.9.16).

Changed — container send-queue limits

  • The published container image now ships queued_send_messages_soft = 2000 and queued_send_messages_hard = 10000, matching the annotated template and the Rust defaults. It shipped 200 and 1000, so every deployment ran a send queue ten times tighter than the documented default while a code search reported 2000, which is a trap for anyone sizing a deployment or reading a queue_max_saturation_ratio against the wrong denominator. 200 is also tight in practice: a sender whose recipients stop deleting fills it in seconds. queued_receive_messages_soft and _hard are unchanged at 200 and 1000, because the receive limits bound total storage and the send limits do not; queued_send_messages_per_peer is unchanged at 50 and remains the gate that catches one sender flooding one recipient.

Fixed

  • A standard account can no longer switch its own queue limit off. Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v5.0.0

🎂 Six years of backport-action

Six years ago today, on November 11, 2020, the first commit of backport-action landed. What started as a small script to save us from cherry-picking by hand has grown into an action trusted by projects of all sizes. Among the public repositories using it, 137 have over 100 stars, 67 have over 1,000, 18 have over 10,000, and 4 have over 100,000. We've had 48 releases, with contributions from 24 people. And we've collected 125 stars ourselves.

Thank you to everyone who contributed code, reported an issue, shared an idea, or simply trusted this action with your backports. A new major release is a fitting way to mark the occasion. Here's to the next six years!

Breaking changes

v5 is all about improving placeholders: the ${...} values the action fills into the pull_title, pull_description and branch_name templates. The default templates use them too. Most workflows won't notice a difference. If you've customized pull_title, pull_description or branch_name, check the notes below.

Every occurrence of a placeholder is replaced

A placeholder that occurs more than once in a template is now replaced everywhere. A template like ${pull_number} ... ${pull_number} now results in 123 ... 123, as you'd expect. Previously it resulted in 123 ... ${pull_number}.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.40.5
body:
### Specifications

- **vtc/rooms/community**: A community-owned room states and changes its signal delay (create 0.5, update 0.4, get 0.5) ([#1336](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1336))

A room a member owns states its signal delay at rooms/create 0.3 and its
  administrators change it at the host with rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1. A
  room the community owns could do neither: the community is both the
  holder of `admin` and the host, and vtc/rooms/community/create and
  update carried no such member, so every community room waited a
  randomised few seconds before each rooms/changed signal however its
  members used it.

  - create 0.5 takes an optional `signalDelay` (absent = randomised),
    records it in the room's host record and always echoes it. A `none`
    create is audited with the create.
  - update 0.4 takes an optional `signalDelay`, applied to the host record
    with the other details, together or not at all; a change of the delay
    alone is a change (audited, details timestamps move) that needs no
    profile write. It touches no watch.
  - get 0.5 always serves the room's `signalDelay`.
  - Both writes refuse `signalDelayNotPermitted` when the community's
    governance as host keeps the delay everywhere, applying nothing.
  - A surface offering `none` SHOULD say what it gives up.

  Links to create 0.4, update 0.3 and get 0.4 move to the new versions.

Updates `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action` from 2.1.1 to 2.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action's releases.

Release 2.1.2 - cargo-deny 0.21.0

Fixed

  • PR#893 resolved #892 by correctly handling url matching when using IP hosts.
  • PR#895 fixed an issue where --target could not be passed multiple times in the CLI.
  • PR#885 resolved #772 by not emitting diagnostics for unused workspace dependencies when those crates were explicitly excluded from the graph by the user.
  • PR#887 resolved #707 by ignoring renamed packages when checking for workspace duplicates.
  • PR#902 resolved #898 by adding the unmatched-allow-build-script and allowed-crate-without-build-script diagnostics.
  • PR#911 resolved #910 by visiting each crate once when checking build-time dependents, so a dependency cycle no longer overflows the stack.
  • PR#915 resolved #914 by ignoring a trailing slash when exactly matching source urls, so that licenses.private.ignore-sources can match sparse registries.

Added

  • PR#899 resolved #896 by searching for configuration in .config as well.
  • PR#904 resolved #754 and #889 by adding 3 new configuration fields:
    • advisories.ignore-expiry - The default duration after the publishing of an advisory that an advisories.ignore will function for it. Once the current date surpasses that expiry the ignore will not prevent the diagnostic for the advisory being emitted. This also accepts an absolute date.
    • advisories.ignore.expiry is the same as the above, but scoped to a particular ignore. This value overrides the default.
    • advisories.ignore.allow only allows specific crates by PackageSpec to depend on the crate(s) that the advisory applies to, intended to prevent new crates or versions from being added to the graph that increase the number of edges and thus making it harder to update/remove the affected crate.
  • PR#906 changed the diagnostics for advisories and yanked crates to conditionally show the (try cargo update -p <affected crate>) and instead detect if any dependents use 1 or more version requirements that preclude updating to an unaffected/patched/unyanked version.

Deprecated

  • PR#903 deprecated the advisories.git-fetch-with-cli configuration field, which has done nothing since PR#830.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.40.4` → `0.40.5` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.31.2` → `0.31.3` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` | npm | `0.2.1` → `0.2.2` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.13.4`) | `0.13.3` → `0.13.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.3`) | `0.1.2` → `0.1.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.2` → `0.12.3` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

v31.0.1

  • Improved performance of computed style reads, selector matching, CSS variable substitution, CSS shorthand updates, and focus handling on pages with many style rules. (@​scttcper)
  • Improved performance when building detached DOM trees and reading node.isConnected. (@​scttcper)

  • Fixed CSS ident() results containing spaces or leading digits losing their required escaping during serialization and variable substitution. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed 'max-lines' values combining an integer and auto to serialize with the integer first, such as 3 auto.

title: fix(vtc): a network that refuses the community is not one that does not list it
body:
**Problem.** The operator console's Networks → Join preview showed "Not listed" and greyed out Join whenever the network refused the community's read of its own entry. SEDI's did:webs VTC hit this: the VTN couldn't resolve did:webs and answered `permissionDenied`, but the console said "This network does not list this community yet… Ask its administrators to invite it first", with the real reason in parentheses. The network had already listed it.

**Server** (`vtc-service/src/networks/mod.rs`): `check_own_entry` classifies the `vtn/entries/show` outcome as a `ListingProblem`:
- `notListed`: the network answered that it has no entry. That's `taskFailed` with `details.reason: not_found` (how a VTN answers), a bare `notFound`, or a declared `…:notListed`.
- `invalidListing`: the network answered, but the listing doesn't verify, or doesn't list this community as a community.
- `refused`: any other refusal, e.g. `permissionDenied` from a network that can't verify the community's signature.
- `unreachable`: a transport error.

The preview response schema (`vtc/networks/preview/0.1`) is closed, so the classification goes in `ext."org.openvtc".listingProblem`, alongside the existing `notListedReason`. Join, repudiate and the other writes now report a refusal as `networkRefused` and no answer as `unavailable`, instead of `notListed`.

**Console** (`admin-ui`, Networks):
- For `refused`, `unreachable` and `invalidListing` it shows an error alert with a headline saying what happened and the network's reason in full. If the reason is an unsupported DID method, it adds: "The network can't resolve this community's DID method. It may need upgrading before this community can join."
- The status chip reads "Network refused", "Couldn't check" or "Listing invalid", in the danger colour.
- `notListed` keeps its existing wording.
- Join stays disabled in every case.
- A VTC that predates this sends no `ext`, and the console reads that as `notListed`, as before.

**Tests:**
- Unit (`networks/tests.rs`): the mock network refuses `vtn/entries/show` with not-found, a declared `notListed`, or `permissionDenied` (the did:webs message). The preview classifies each one, and join reports the refusal as `Refused`. The classification rules have their own unit test.
- Integration (`tests/it/networks.rs`): the mock's "not listed" now answers the way a real VTN does (not-found), and a new `deny` switch refuses with `permissionDenied`. The preview's `ext` gives `notListed` and `refused` respectively, and the existing join and repudiate `notListed` assertions still hold.
- Vitest (`Networks.test.tsx`): covers the refused state with the DID-method hint, the unreachable state without the hint, "not listed" showing no alert, and `listingProblemOf`, including an old VTC with no `ext`.

title: feat(landing): verify did:webs signers in the browser with vti-didcomm-js's resolver
body:
"Verify a member" on the landing page couldn't resolve did:webs. So a did:webs community's acknowledgement, e.g. the SEDI VTC's, showed "signature not checked here: cannot resolve did:webs here".

**What changes**
- `vtn-service/web/did-webs.js` (181 KB, generated): the `./did-webs` resolver from `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` 0.16.1, bundled into one browser ES module with esbuild 0.28.2. It does CESR parsing, key event log verification and key-role designations. Its only runtime dependencies are `@noble/curves` and `@noble/hashes` (MIT), approved for bundling. The file's header names the source, the versions and the licences.
- `scripts/vendor-did-webs.sh` regenerates it from the pins in `vtn-service/web/vendor/package.json`. It installs and bundles in a temporary directory, never in the repository.
- The VTN serves the module at `/web/did-webs.js` (`include_str!`, `text/javascript`, cached for a day). The page imports it only when it meets a did:webs signer. The CSP gains `script-src 'self'` for it, and nothing is loaded from a third party.
- `verifyProof` accepts an Ed25519 OKP `publicKeyJwk` (what did:webs documents carry) as well as a multikey. did:webvh and did:key behave as before.

**Checked**
- CORS: `https://webvh.storm.ws` serves SEDI's `did.json` and `keri.cesr` with `access-control-allow-origin: *`.
- The page's own `resolveDid` and `verifyProof` code, run in Node against the live `/v1/index`: SEDI's real acknowledgement gives `ok: true`, a tampered copy gives `the signature does not verify`, and the wrong purpose is refused.
- Route test: the module is served with the right content type and the CSP admits it.

title: fix!: verify every VTA reply, and sign the TSP announce
body:
This is the app side of OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1744. It follows two VTI changes:

- #1739: the VTA and the VTC accept a Trust Task over DIDComm or TSP only when its proof verifies as its `issuer`, and that issuer is the transport sender.
- #1740: every VTA and VTC response, errors included, is signed under `proofPurpose: authentication`.

## What the app sends

The app already sent only signed documents built by the engine: `whoami`, step-up approve/deny, task-consent approve/deny and `device/set-wake`, each with a fresh `urn:uuid` id, `issuedAt`, `issuer` set to the device `did:key` and `recipient` set to the VTA. With #1744 the engine:

- signs these under `authentication`, except the approver's own decisions: the step-up `approve-response` and the `task-consent/decision` (approve and deny for each). These are evidence the executor records, so they are signed under `assertionMethod`, and only with a key the device's `did:key` lists there;
- refuses to send any document that is unsigned, or is not issued by this holder to this VTA.

The one unsigned document was the TSP reachability announce, an unsigned `messaging/ping/0.1` that #1739 refuses. It is replaced by `VtaMobileAgent.announceTsp`, which sends a holder-signed ping. The engine's `announce` is removed.

The app sends none of the legacy DIDComm protocol messages that #1739 removes. It uses only the Trust Task envelope over DIDComm and the TSP binding envelope.

## Pushed approval requests

The step-up approve-request, consent request and task-consent request the VTA pushes are its operational messages. #1740 signs them with the operational key under `authentication`, and the #1744 engine refuses one signed under `assertionMethod`, or with a key the issuer does not list under `authentication`, before it prompts. The signed step-up fixtures in `AuthorizationContextTests` are re-signed under `authentication` with the same deterministic test key (seed 17). They were re-signed and checked with the engine's `verify_signed_request` in a throwaway Rust test.

## How replies are verified

| Transport | Where | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| DIDComm | engine, inside `MediatorSession.sendTrustTask` | proof by the VTA under `authentication` (key listed under `authentication`); `threadId` and `type` answer the request; issued by the VTA to this device |
| TSP | `TspReplyRouter.deliver`, via `verifyTrustTaskReply` | same, checked **before** the waiting `submit` is resolved |

Over TSP, a frame that echoes a `threadId` but fails verification is not consumed. The expectation stays open, so the genuine reply still resolves the submit, and a reply that never verifies times out. Error replies must verify too.

## Also

- Re-vendors `Sources/VtaMobileCore/VtaMobileCore.swift`, generated from the #1744 engine. The diff is large because the generator on main has moved on since the v0.6.17 release was vendored.
- The `Package.swift` pin TODO now points at #1744. Until a `vta-mobile-core-v*` release is cut from #1744 and the tag and checksum here are bumped, a checkout needs the local-xcframework override. **CI on this PR is expected to fail until then**: the v0.6.17 binary does not match the vendored bindings, and it still expects pushed requests under `assertionMethod`. No release is cut as part of this PR.
- The README and doc comments describe proof-bound requests and verified replies instead of intrinsic-sender auth, and the exception for the approver's decisions.

## Verification

No full Xcode is installed on the machine this was prepared on (Command Line Tools only), so `xcodebuild test` on a simulator and the XCTest suite were **not** run. What was run:

- `swiftc -typecheck` of `Sources/VtaMobileCore` and `Sources/VtaMobileAgent` against the regenerated bindings and FFI header (macOS target): clean.
- `App/` type-checked for Mac Catalyst (`arm64-apple-ios16.0-macabi`): clean apart from the `#Preview` macro, whose plugin ships only with Xcode.
- A throwaway macOS executable linking the host build of the #1744 engine, exercising the router and the real verifier. All checks passed:
  - a forged reply is not consumed, and the genuine reply resolves the waiter;
  - an unexpected thread passes through;
  - a reply that never verifies times out;
  - the engine refuses an unsigned reply with `UnverifiedReply`;
  - the default router does not consume an unsigned reply.
- The updated `TspReplyRouterTests`, including three new cases for these rules, and the re-signed `AuthorizationContextTests` fixtures were written but not compiled, since XCTest is unavailable here (`swiftc -parse` only).

Not run: an end-to-end test against a deployed VTA built from #1739 and #1740.

title: fix(vta-mobile-core): keep `/*` out of doc comments so the Swift bindings compile
body:
UniFFI copies doc comments into the generated Swift as block comments, and Swift nests block comments. Six exported doc comments in vta-mobile-core named a task family as `vta/pcs/*` or `vta/witness/*`. Each `/*` opened a comment that never closed, so the generated `VtaMobileCore.swift` for 0.6.18 did not compile until it was edited by hand (vta-mobile-agent-ios#29, commit ca9c6f6).

- Task families are now written `vta/pcs/<task>`, `vta/witness/<task>` and `auth/<task>`: 11 lines in all, including module docs for consistency. No API change.
- New test `vta-mobile-core/tests/doc_comments.rs` fails if any doc comment in the crate's `src/` contains `/*` or `*/`, so the next release's bindings compile as generated.

vta-mobile-core is the only crate in the workspace that uses UniFFI.

title: feat(service): trust extra_root_certificates for status-list fetches when private endpoints are allowed
body:
vtn-service loaded `extra_root_certificates` into its own HTTP client, but never gave them to vta-sdk's hardened foreign-fetch client. That client fetches status lists, because their URLs come from credentials. Behind a private CA, every status check therefore came back indeterminate. #37 worked around this in the tests only.

**Change** (`vtn-service/src/lib.rs`): at startup, after the configured PEM bundles are parsed (an unreadable or non-PEM file still fails startup with its path), the roots go to `vta_sdk::http::set_private_extra_root_certificates`. That happens only when the process allows private endpoints (`VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`, read through `EndpointPolicy::process_default()`, the same policy vti-vtn's client uses), the only policy under which vta-sdk trusts extra roots. An info log records how many roots were applied, or why none were.

**Config:** the existing `extra_root_certificates`, plus the `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` environment variable. Nothing new. The doc comment in `config.rs`, `vtn.example.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` explain it.

**Test:** a unit test checks that roots are applied under the private policy, left out under the public-only one, and that an empty list changes nothing.

Follows OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2776 (#2773).

checks a network's own status list, at its base_url, and a network's
base_url must stay https (it is also the relay endpoint groups::register
requires). That case needs the hardened client to trust extra roots (VTI

#2773).

title: vtc-service-v0.32.0
body: ### Added - **vtc-service**: Serve the landing page from a directory (website.landing_dir) ([#2767](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2767)) A community wanting its own landing page had two choices: edit website-default/ and rebuild the daemon, or set website.root_dir, which must sit on a host of its own because administrators can deploy into it over the network. website.landing_dir is a third: a directory the host operator places, served at the website mount in place of the built-in page and re-read on every request, so an edit shows on the next load with no rebuild and no restart. Nothing over the network writes it (the /v1/website/* tasks act only on root_dir), so it is as trusted as the operator and may share the console's origin, the footing admin_ui.dir already has. Boot refuses one without a readable index.html or that is world-writable (the check is now shared with admin_ui.dir / members_dir as website::paths::check_operator_dir); naming both root_dir and landing_dir is refused. Paths go through the website's safety chain. `vtc website export ` writes the built-in page out to start from. - **vtc-service**: Serve vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 so the console seals for any DID method ([#2762](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2762)) * feat(vtc-service): serve vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 so the console seals for any DID method The console sealed a storage credential to the key it read from the community's same-origin /.well-known/did.jsonl. A did:webs community serves no log, so sealing always failed and the console fell back to `cnm`. A did:webvh community on a DID host failed the same way. The community now answers vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1329): - It returns the Ed25519 key it opens sealed blocks with, as a did:key, plus the verification method that publishes it (item 2). - When its own DID resolves, the answer is checked against that document. If the document publishes a different signing key, the answer is `notPublished` (retryable) and carries no key, so nothing is sealed to a key that has rotated away (item 3). - It requires `vtc.rooms.admin`, the same authority as credentials/set (item 1). The console asks this task instead of reading did.jsonl. It accepts the answer only when it names the community's own DID (item 4) and seals to it as given (item 5). - **vtc-service**: Store and serve an uploaded community logo ([#2751](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2751)) * feat(vtc-service): store and serve an uploaded community logo A community can now upload its logo, and the VTC serves it from its own origin, so it shows in the console, the member portal, both sign-in pages and the default landing page wherever the VTC is hosted. Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. What it adds: - `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1` (pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`): an administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one re-encoding at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - `GET /v1/community/logo`: public, like `public-profile`. Served from memory against a small record read, with a fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - A `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - Console: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. Design note: docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md. ### Fixed - **vtc-service**: Setup speaks did:webs, not webvh, once the operator chooses it ([#2760](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2760)) The interactive wizard asked "WebVH path (blank → server-assigned)" and described the path as the DID's trailing segment after a did:webs choice. A did:webs path is the slot before the AID, and blank publishes at the domain's top level. The path prompt now follows the chosen method and refuses `.well-known` for a did:webs, as `vtc setup --from` and the VTA do. The hosting intro presents both DID shapes instead of did:webvh alone. The same webvh-only advice for changing the document after mint (the registry prompt, the `registry_did` and `[webvh]` docs, the example setup TOML, community-lifecycle.md) now gives the did:webs route as well. - **vtc-service**: Vtc setup finds a TSP-only VTA's mediator ([#2755](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2755)) The setup wizard suggested only the mediator from the VTA's `DIDCommMessaging` service, so a VTA advertising only `TSPTransport` was reported as having no mediator. The suggestion now reads the TSP entry first and the DIDComm entry second (TSP > DIDComm), naming the transports the VTA uses it for, and the prompt's wording is transport-neutral. The did-hosting picker's connect had the same gap: without REST it tried only DIDComm. It now connects over TSP before DIDComm. - **vtc-service**: Setup never mints a did:webvh for an operator who chose did:webs ([#2756](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2756)) When the interactive wizard could not read the VTA's did-hosting catalogue (for example against a TSP-only VTA, which the catalogue client could not reach), it returned `IdentityMethod::Webvh` before asking for the method, so an operator who wanted a did:webs got a did:webvh with only a printed line to say so. The method is now asked in every case. Without the catalogue, a did:webvh is still left to the VTA's own server pick; a did:webs, which needs a named server and has no serverless mode, is refused with the fix: `vtc setup --from` with `identity_method = "webs"` and `[webvh] server_id`. ### Performance - Use jemalloc in every service binary so freed memory returns to the OS ([#2758](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2758)) The service binaries ran on the system allocator. glibc malloc keeps freed pages in its arenas instead of returning them, so a service's RSS ratchets up to its high-water mark and stays there; on a memory graph that is indistinguishable from a leak (the VTC in particular has been climbing). vtc, vta, vta-enclave, vti-witness, room-host and vti-voting-service now set tikv-jemallocator as the global allocator behind a default-on `jemalloc` feature (non-MSVC only), matching the mediator. jemalloc is tuned through the exported `_rjem_malloc_conf` symbol: background_thread:true (purge while idle) and 5s dirty/muzzy decay. The symbol must carry the `_rjem_` prefix tikv-jemalloc-sys builds with; an unprefixed `malloc_conf` is silently ignored. Both Dockerfiles build with --no-default-features, so they append `jemalloc` to FEATURES for every profile. Each crate now carries the deny-not-forbid unsafe_code lint table for the one exported static, and is listed in scripts/check-workspace-lints.py.

title: vta-service-v0.84.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*) ([#2763](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2763))

* feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*)

- **vta-signing**: A small signing library the VTA and its callers share ([#2745](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2745))

* feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types

  Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over
  a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike
  `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the
  `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under
  `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than
  as a VTA opaque-signing payload.

  The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or
  issuer artifact:

  - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT
    profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`);
    anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before
    the key is touched;
  - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request
    a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one;
  - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go
    through the opaque oracle, not here.

  Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same
  context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the
  dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and
  acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any
  unknown-schema task until then).

  Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG)
  to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from
  credential signing.



### Documentation

- **design-notes**: DID management, one question asked once whatever the method ([#2761](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2761))

Records the split between method-neutral DID questions (vta/dids list,
  get, methods/list; a context's DID through update-did 1.2) and the
  per-method operations that stay in their families; the DidEngine seam in
  vta-service; and the rules the webvh and webs paths had drifted on.

  Also corrects three stale statements found in the review: the did:webs
  note's section 1 table, which section 4 had overtaken (did:webs is a
  service-DID method since dtgwg-vti-spec#121/#123); pnm's 'never a node's
  own identity' help text; and the webvh handler header, which listed
  retired URIs and wrong auth for domains and agent names.



### Fixed

- **vta-service**: A key-role did:webs signs with the key of the proof's purpose ([#2766](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2766))

A key-role did:webs publishes a different key for each relationship
  (VTI-KEY-072): its operational key under authentication, its attestation
  key under assertionMethod, and the key event log's own key under neither.
  Two places assumed one signing key per identity:

  - vault/sign-trust-task signed every document with the entry's one stored
    signingKeyId. A wallet sign-in signs auth/oob/identify for authentication
    and auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod, so a community refused one of the
    two whichever key the entry named (VTI-KEY-022). Where the principal is a
    key-role did:webs this agent holds, the purpose now decides the key; every
    other principal still signs with the entry's key. The key is still held to
    the entry's context (custody rule 7).
  - vta/dids/list reported the key event log's key as signingKeyId, which a
    client then stored in the entry: a method the document lists nowhere. It
    now reports the operational key for a key-role identity.

  persona_key_for also answers for a key-role did:webs, with the role key of
  the relationship, checked against the identity's own document and held to
  the same record checks as a level-1 identity.

- **vta-service**: Refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:w… ([#2765](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2765))

* fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:webvh update key

  A VTA-built did:webvh uses one key as its signing key and its log's update
  key. keys/sign-document signed a caller's document as the did:key of any key in
  the caller's scope, so a holder of sign-document in the context could have the
  update key sign a forged log entry (a proof by did:key:<update key> is exactly a
  log entry's) that adds its own key to the DID, and keep that key after its grant
  is revoked.

  sign-document now refuses to sign as a did:key whose key is an active update or
  pre-rotation key of a did:webvh this VTA holds. The key still signs as the
  did:webvh it serves, whose proofs name that DID's own method.

- **vta-service**: Check a did:webs publication against the host's didId, not didUrl ([#2752](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2752))

`did-management/did/register/0.1` defines a `DidRecord`'s `didUrl` as the URL
  of the slot's log document and `didId` as the identifier the host derived from
  it. Publishing a did:webs compared `didUrl` with the DID, so every real host's
  answer was refused: a did:webs VTA's first boot published its identity, then
  refused to record it ("the hosting server published https://…/did.jsonl for
  slot …, not did:webs:…"), and `pnm webs create` would refuse the same way.
  The test hosts put the DID in `didUrl`, so no test caught it.

  `RequestUriResponse` carries the record's `didId` as `did_id`, and both the
  own-identity publish and create check it. The test hosts answer as a host
  does: `didUrl` the log's URL, `didId` the identifier.

- **vta-service**: A TSP-only VTA boots (#937 follow-up) ([#2743](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2743))

#937 let a VTA speak TSP without DIDComm: setup accepts TSP alone, and the
  mediator connect supervisor opens for `services.didcomm || services.tsp`.
  Two places in `server::run` were missed, so a TSP-only VTA set up that way
  refused to start with "no services enabled — enable at least one of REST or
  DIDComm":

  - The pre-loop guard, and the restart loop's warning, counted only REST and
    DIDComm. Both now ask `any_transport_enabled`, which counts REST, DIDComm
    or TSP, each built and enabled. WebAuthn alone is still not a transport.
  - `services.tsp` was migrated into the runtime state on first boot but never
    mirrored back at boot or on a soft restart, unlike REST and DIDComm, so
    `pnm services tsp {enable,disable}` did not survive a restart. It is now
    mirrored in both places, before the unbuilt-TSP check reads it.



### Performance

- Use jemalloc in every service binary so freed memory returns to the OS ([#2758](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2758))

The service binaries ran on the system allocator. glibc malloc keeps freed
  pages in its arenas instead of returning them, so a service's RSS ratchets
  up to its high-water mark and stays there; on a memory graph that is
  indistinguishable from a leak (the VTC in particular has been climbing).

  vtc, vta, vta-enclave, vti-witness, room-host and vti-voting-service now
  set tikv-jemallocator as the global allocator behind a default-on
  `jemalloc` feature (non-MSVC only), matching the mediator. jemalloc is
  tuned through the exported `_rjem_malloc_conf` symbol:
  background_thread:true (purge while idle) and 5s dirty/muzzy decay.
  The symbol must carry the `_rjem_` prefix tikv-jemalloc-sys builds with;
  an unprefixed `malloc_conf` is silently ignored.

  Both Dockerfiles build with --no-default-features, so they append
  `jemalloc` to FEATURES for every profile. Each crate now carries the
  deny-not-forbid unsafe_code lint table for the one exported static, and
  is listed in scripts/check-workspace-lints.py.

title: vtc-client-v0.46.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vtc-client**: Send_task keeps a refusal's document over a session ([#2768](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2768))

send_task promised VtcError::Refused over a session, carrying the
  trust-task-error document, but sent through the typed `document` helper,
  which asks the session for the payload alone and turns a refusal into a
  one-line VtcError::Session. A generic caller acts on what that drops: a
  refusal's details carry the step-up the community asks the person for
  (stepUpHandoff, VTI-LNK-125 - 131).

  Seen through vtc-mcp: vtc/rooms/community/create answered "a passkey
  gesture bound to this operation is required" as a transport error, with no
  link for the person's wallet, so an administrator with an enrolled approver
  could not answer the step-up at all.

  Over a session send_task now asks for the reply document and reads it as
  the HTTPS path reads one: a trust-task-error is NotFound where it carries
  one of the task's declared codes saying the thing is absent, else Refused
  with the document as received; a next-step is Parked; a response is its
  payload. The typed methods are unchanged.

* feat(vtc-service): serve vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 so the console seals for any DID method

  community's same-origin /.well-known/did.jsonl. A did:webs community
  serves no log, so sealing always failed and the console fell back to
  `cnm`. A did:webvh community on a DID host failed the same way.

  The community now answers vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1329):
  - It returns the Ed25519 key it opens sealed blocks with, as a did:key,
    plus the verification method that publishes it (item 2).
  - When its own DID resolves, the answer is checked against that
    document. If the document publishes a different signing key, the
    answer is `notPublished` (retryable) and carries no key, so nothing
    is sealed to a key that has rotated away (item 3).
  - It requires `vtc.rooms.admin`, the same authority as credentials/set
    (item 1).

  The console asks this task instead of reading did.jsonl. It accepts the
  answer only when it names the community's own DID (item 4) and seals to
  it as given (item 5).

- **vta**: Every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*) ([#2763](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2763))

* feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*)

- **vta-signing**: A small signing library the VTA and its callers share ([#2745](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2745))

* feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types

  Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over
  a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike
  `keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the
  `b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under
  `SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than
  as a VTA opaque-signing payload.

  The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or
  issuer artifact:

  - the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT
    profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`);
    anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before
    the key is touched;
  - the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request
    a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one;
  - the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go
    through the opaque oracle, not here.

  Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same
  context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the
  dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and
  acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any
  unknown-schema task until then).

  Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG)
  to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from
  credential signing.

A did:webs community serves no log, so sealing always failed and the console fell back to `cnm`. A did:webvh community on a DID host failed the same way. The community now answers vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1329): - It returns the Ed25519 key it opens sealed blocks with, as a did:key, plus the verification method that publishes it (item 2). - When its own DID resolves, the answer is checked against that document. If the document publishes a different signing key, the answer is `notPublished` (retryable) and carries no key, so nothing is sealed to a key that has rotated away (item 3). - It requires `vtc.rooms.admin`, the same authority as credentials/set (item 1). The console asks this task instead of reading did.jsonl. It accepts the answer only when it names the community's own DID (item 4) and seals to it as given (item 5). - **vtc-service**: Store and serve an uploaded community logo ([#2751](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2751)) * feat(vtc-service): store and serve an uploaded community logo A community can now upload its logo, and the VTC serves it from its own origin, so it shows in the console, the member portal, both sign-in pages and the default landing page wherever the VTC is hosted. Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. What it adds: - `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1` (pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`): an administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one re-encoding at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - `GET /v1/community/logo`: public, like `public-profile`. Served from memory against a small record read, with a fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - A `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - Console: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. Design note: docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md.

title: feat(vta-sdk): trust extra root certificates under the private endpoint policy
body:
Closes #2773.

`vta_sdk::http::set_private_extra_root_certificates(roots)` is a process-wide setter, like `set_allow_private_endpoints`. It sets roots that the hardened foreign-fetch client trusts **only under `EndpointPolicy::private_allowed`**:

- **Public-only:** unchanged. `foreign_fetch_client()` and `foreign_fetch_client_for(public_only)` are the same static client, trusting the system roots alone.
- **Private policy:** the client is built on first use, as before, and now rebuilt after the roots change. Redirects, proxying, the guarded resolver and the timeouts are unchanged.
- **vti-vtn:** `VtnClient::get_url`, the status-list fetch, already uses that client, so it gets the roots without an API change. Only its doc comment changes.

The motivating case is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network#37: a network whose status lists sit behind a private CA, including its tests' own CA, can't have them checked today.

Tests: `private_extra_roots_are_set_replaced_and_cleared` uses a real rcgen CA (rcgen is already a dev-dependency). It covers building with an extra root, setting, replacing and clearing the roots, rebuilding the cached client, and the public-only path leaving them alone. VTN #37 will exercise it end to end over TLS.
author: stormer78

title: feat(vta-sdk): trust extra root certificates under the private endpoint policy (#2776)
body:
feat(vta-sdk): trust extra root certificates under the private endpoint policy (#2776)

* feat(vta-sdk): trust extra root certificates under the private endpoint policy

The hardened foreign-fetch client trusted the system roots only, and
nothing could add one. A deployment that serves its status lists behind a
private CA, which already needs the private-endpoint opt-in to reach its
own hosts, could not have them checked: every status check failed at the
TLS handshake and verification came back indeterminate.

vta_sdk::http::set_private_extra_root_certificates(roots) sets, for the
rest of the process, roots the private-policy client trusts beside the
system's. It is a process-wide setter beside set_allow_private_endpoints.
The public-only client never uses them, so a process that hasn't opted in
to private endpoints is unaffected. The private client is now built on
first use and rebuilt after the roots change. Redirects, proxying, the
guarded resolver and the timeouts are unchanged.

vti-vtn's VtnClient::get_url, the status-list fetch, already uses that
client, so it picks the roots up as is; its documentation now says so.

Closes #2773

title: build: Rust 1.100.0 for the release branch's CI and images
body:
Backport of main's toolchain pin (#2658, landed in #2709), reduced to the part a release branch needs: a `rust-toolchain.toml`.

**Why:** every CI job here runs `rustup toolchain install stable` under `-D warnings`. A new stable release's lints can therefore turn the branch red with no code change. That happened in #2772: the branch had never run CI since it was cut, and Rust 1.100's lints needed three fix-up commits. rustup honours `rust-toolchain.toml` over the `rustup default stable` the workflows run, so no workflow change is needed.

**Why 1.95.0, not main's 1.100.0:** that is the branch's `rust-version` and the `RUST_VERSION` both Dockerfiles build with. CI then builds with the same compiler as the images this branch ships, which is the rule main's pin follows.

**Why release-direct:** main's pin came in with the much larger CI-hardening PR #2709, which can't be cherry-picked onto this branch.

title: feat: /livez and /readyz probes on the VTA and VTC
body:
Adds Kubernetes-style probes beside the unchanged /health, on both
services' REST listeners, outside auth, rate limiting, tracing and the
VTC's host/surface gate:

- GET /livez answers 200 {"status":"ok"} while the server answers and
  checks nothing else, so storage trouble or an unreachable mediator
  never gets a healthy process restarted.
- GET /readyz answers 200 {"status":"ready","storage":"ok"}, or 503
  {"status":"notReady","storage":"unavailable"} while the store is
  unavailable. The mediator is deliberately not checked: messaging has
  its own reconnect supervisor and REST callers are served without it.

The store check is KeyspaceHandle::probe: for fjall, the data directory
still holds the database (an open database keeps answering from memory
after its volume goes) and the journal accepts a flush to OS buffers
(fails once fjall has poisoned the database); for the enclave's vsock
store, one read round trip to the parent proxy. It never writes or
fsyncs, is bounded at 800 ms, and vti_common::health::ReadinessProbe
caches its answer for 1 s so unauthenticated callers cause at most one
check a second. Causes are logged, never put in the body.

Docs: docs/04-reference/health-probes.md, with a probe example.

Requested by a Kubernetes deployer who already uses the mediator's `/mediator/v1/livez` and `/readyz`. The matching change for DID Hosting is in affinidi-webvh-service.

Tests: `vti_common::health` unit tests (ready, data directory deleted under an open store → 503, cache window), plus a route test on each service. Workspace nextest, VTC nextest, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and `check-docs.py` all pass locally; the one workspace failure, `vti-rooms blobs::migrate::tests::a_failure_short_of_the_cap_backs_off_running`, is timing-sensitive under load and passes 3/3 when run alone.

Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.2

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 7.30.1 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

In Undici 7.x, the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

Undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] fix(decompress): join a repeated content-encoding header (#5664) by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6026
  • ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6087
  • fix(h1): backport ignore type of service errors to v7.x (#5547) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6076
  • [Backport v7.x] extractBody fixes 2 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#6093

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.30.1...v7.30.2

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.2

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 7.30.1 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

In Undici 7.x, the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

Undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] fix(decompress): join a repeated content-encoding header (#5664) by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6026
  • ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6087
  • fix(h1): backport ignore type of service errors to v7.x (#5547) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6076
  • [Backport v7.x] extractBody fixes 2 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#6093

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.30.1...v7.30.2

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

title: fix(deps): patch the RustSec advisories open on release/eucalyptus
body:
Fixes the `cargo deny advisories (release/eucalyptus)` failure in the daily advisory scan (#2729). `main` passes; Eucalyptus is the supported N release, so its security fixes have to land here.

## Why `release-direct`, not a backport

`main` reached these versions through many lockfile-wide PRs (dependabot groups such as #2392, plus the rustls, rmcp and tokio bumps). None of them cherry-picks onto this branch's lockfile. This PR moves the branch's `Cargo.lock` to the versions `main` already runs, so it adds no change `main` hasn't already tested.

## What changes

**Patched versions** (all semver-compatible, `Cargo.lock` only):

| Crate | From → To | Advisories |
|---|---|---|
| rustls | 0.23.45 → 0.23.46 | RUSTSEC-2026-0346, 0347, 0348, 0349 |
| rustls-webpki | 0.103.15 → 0.103.16 | 0382 |
| webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs | 1.0.9 → 1.0.10 | 0381, 0383 |
| ctutils | 0.4.2 → 0.4.8 | 0385 |
| crypto-bigint (0.7 line) | 0.7.5 → 0.7.11 | 0387 (0.7.5 was also yanked) |
| tokio | 1.53.1 → 1.53.3 | 0386 |
| rmcp | 3.5.0 → 3.9.0 | 0457, 0461, 0462 |
| url | 2.5.8 → 2.5.9 | 0592 |

**pin-utils (RUSTSEC-2026-0441, unmaintained):** aws-smithy-http dropped it in 0.64.2. That needs aws-smithy-types 1.9, so the workspace bound moves from `<1.9` to `<1.10`, exactly as on `main` (#2392). The AWS SDK crates are pinned to `main`'s exact versions (aws-config 1.13.0, aws-sdk-* as on `main`).

**Ignored with `main`'s own `deny.toml` entries, unchanged:** zip 2.x (0367, 0368, 0369, 0429, 0545, 0548), basic-toml (0374), crypto-bigint 0.5 (0387), chrono (0543), chrono-tz (0555) and humantime (0542). Each reaches this branch by the same path `main`'s reason describes:
- zip: only `nitro_attest`'s build script
- basic-toml: `askama_derive` under uniffi
- crypto-bigint 0.5.5: `elliptic-curve` 0.13 and rPGP
- chrono-tz: regorus
- humantime: the mediator

## Checked

`cargo deny --all-features check` passes locally: advisories, bans, licenses and sources are all ok. No crate `version` changes; the next prep PR assigns patch versions.

title: chore(deps)!: move to the affinidi-tdk 0.49 generation
body:
Replaces #46, which bumped only the affinidi-tdk dev-dependency (to 0.37, now well out of date). That left two affinidi-crypto versions in the tree through trust-tasks-proof, so the build failed.

**What changes:**
- `affinidi-data-integrity` 0.8 → 0.9
- `affinidi-secrets-resolver` 0.5 → 0.6
- `affinidi-did-common` 0.4.4 → 0.5
- `affinidi-tdk` (dev) 0.36 → 0.49

With these, a fresh resolve has no duplicate affinidi or DID crates (`cargo tree -d`), with one affinidi-crypto at 0.4.

**Breaking:** `DataIntegrityProof`, `SignOptions`, `VerifyOptions` and `Secret` appear in this crate's API, so callers need the same generation. This is noted under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md, and the version bump is left for the release commit, as with earlier dependency moves.

It also fixes the rustfmt drift in `src/create.rs` and `src/lib.rs` that was failing the Format check.

No source changes were needed: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean.
